events.text: Sirin the barge-singer has a new ballad, and tonight it is about {llg_who}, who lived to {llg_told_age} and left {llg_thing} in {llg_region}. "My aunt hung its first lantern," Sirin tells the quay, tapping the drum in a slow march. The tune is plain. You find yourself leaning against a mooring post long after the crowd has gone home.

choices.text: Ask Sirin where the lanterns hang now

effects.log: Sirin sketches the isle on the back of a ticket and wants a copper for it. You pay, and keep the ticket in your sleeve.

choices.text: Leave a copper in the drum and drift on

effects.log: The drum answers with one soft beat. The name stays with you, a small stone in a shoe.

events.text: Sirin sings it with both arms raised and the drum between the knees: when {llg_who} first reached {llg_region}, the tide of cloud drew back like a curtain, and {llg_thing} was built where it parted. "{llg_He} lived {llg_told_age} years," she sings, "and never once looked down." You think the verse is absurd, and your throat tightens anyway.

choices.text: Mutter that nobody can live without looking down

effects.log: Sirin catches it and cheers, and the quay roars. For one breath it feels as if you had once tried.

choices.text: Ask what the hall looks like today

effects.log: Cracked paint and sweet incense, she says, and a queue for the rain-prayers. Most of the prayers go unanswered, and the queue stays long.

events.text: The new almanac for pilots has a mountain on it that was nameless last year: {llg_thing}, after {llg_who}. An old pilot, mending a rope, says {llg_he} died of {llg_cause}, and that the name was carried up from the lower isles on a rumour. He does not look up from the rope. You find you have read the line four times.

choices.text: Ask the pilot what {llg_he} was like

effects.log: "Loud," he says. "Or very quiet. One of the two." You laugh, startled by how glad it makes you.

choices.text: Copy the name into the margin of your own chart

effects.log: The ink smears on the first damp morning. By then you have said the name over so many times it no longer needs the chart.

events.text: Cloud-children count the peaks of {llg_region} in a skipping rhyme, and {llg_Thing} always lands on the third beat. Nobody asks what the word means until a boy of twelve does, and his grandmother says it was a word for some great beast, from the days before the isles rose. You are sure, at once and for no reason, that she has it wrong.

choices.text: Chant the rhyme again, slower, until the word falls apart

effects.log: It falls apart, and a half-sense is left in the pieces. You put it away carefully, the way you would a bird.

choices.text: Rejoin the skipping and miss on the third beat

effects.log: The rope catches your ankle exactly there. The children shriek with pleasure, and you will never get it right now.

events.text: A lame sword-immortal, warming his hands at the terrace brazier, says he learned the opening forms at {llg_thing} in {llg_region}, from a master whose master had known {llg_who}, {llg_years} years gone. "Worn hollows in the flagstones," he says. "Set your heels in them." You look down and find your heels already there.

choices.text: Ask him to walk the first form for you

effects.log: He walks it wrong, swears, and walks it again. You catch the fault before he does, and neither of you can say where you learned it.

choices.text: Refill his cup and let him ramble

effects.log: He ranges across fifty years of sword-gossip. The hollows in the flagstones come up in every version.

events.text: At the Lantern Fair the swordsmiths tell it that all blade-craft began at {llg_thing} in {llg_region}, when a sky-spirit and a cliff fell out, and the spirit has ever since gone by the name {llg_who}. The Jade Court has a shelf of commentaries. The fair has a spiced bun with a swordsman pressed into the crust.

choices.text: Buy the bun

effects.log: The pressed swordsman is a clumsy likeness. You study the feet while you eat, and the feet are wrong, and you cannot tell how you know.

choices.text: Ask who taught the spirit

effects.log: The baker wheezes with laughter and has to sit on a crate. You were serious, and it takes a while to be forgiven for that.

events.text: A ballad is making the rounds of the ferry-landings, "{llg_song}", and the line that sticks is "{llg_verse}". It tells of {llg_who}, gone at {llg_told_age} of {llg_cause}, or so the girl at the oar swears. You have never heard it before. The next line is already in your mouth, and she sings it differently, and you flinch.

choices.text: Sing your own next line quietly beside her

effects.log: She breaks off and stares. "Where did you get that?" You have no answer, and she offers you a rice-ball as if to a stray.

choices.text: Hum along to her version and pay the fare

effects.log: The tune is a good one. You carry it for days, and it does you nothing but good.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} is now a three-evening serial at the floating theatre. In the first, {llg_he} outwits a storm. In the second {llg_he} loves a crane, or a courtier, depending on the troupe. In the third {llg_he} dies of {llg_cause} at {llg_told_age} while the cast sings. You are in tears, and you think the whole thing a foolish piece of work.

choices.text: Come back for the second and third evenings

effects.log: The week is gone before you notice. The crane is the best of it. You have no memory of a crane, which feels like a loss.

choices.text: Ask the stage-manager how much of it happened

effects.log: "Everything," she says, "once it has been told enough." You turn that over for a long time and find you agree.

events.text: In {llg_region} they begin each task the same way, and have for {llg_years} years: two fingers to the brow, one breath held, then the first stroke. A child tells you it is "how it goes". Nobody remembers who began it. You watch twice, and notice two fingers resting against your own brow.

choices.text: Ask the child to teach you the whole of it

effects.log: She does, sternly, and you finish better than she does. She decides you must have had a tutor from the place, and you let her.

choices.text: Lower your hand and walk on

effects.log: You do. Your fingers keep wanting to go back up all week, and you let them stay down.

events.text: On {llg_region} the custom is so ordinary that nobody can name it, the way no one names the colour of air. Scholars at the Jade Court have it older than the isles. Not one of them suggests it came from a person. You catch yourself doing it in a doorway, and you have never been within a hundred leagues.

choices.text: Do it on purpose and see how it feels

effects.log: It feels very right, which is unfair. You are cheerful for no reason all that afternoon.

choices.text: Keep your hands in your sleeves and think of dinner

effects.log: You think of dinner. Your hands, inside the sleeves, are still doing it.

events.text: After the evening bell they stop saying the name {llg_who} in {llg_region}. Sirin will, for double, behind a curtain: how {llg_he} closed a fist on the isles, how {llg_thing} was shut up, and how it has stayed shut for {llg_years} years because nobody wants to learn what answers if it is opened. Your mouth goes dry. You pay without haggling.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} actually did

effects.log: She gives you a short, dreadful account. You sleep badly for a week, and the name sounds more and more like your own.

choices.text: Say that it was very long ago

effects.log: It was. Nobody thanks you for saying so, and you leave the curtain quicker than you meant to.

events.text: Cloud-pilots call a patch of the sky over {llg_region} the Dead Pocket, and the charts mark {llg_thing} beneath it. Nobody flies through. They say {llg_who} did something to the people below, {llg_years} years ago or more, and nobody will say what. They study the rigging while they don't say it, and you study it with them.

choices.text: Ask the pilots what {llg_he} did

effects.log: One of them tells you, haltingly, and stops at the worst part. You do not sleep well for some nights, and cannot say why it feels familiar.

choices.text: Remark that it was a long time ago

effects.log: It was. The pilots go quiet, and you take the next barge out, more quickly than politeness allows.

events.text: Among the sword-immortals the tale of {llg_who} has lost its thunder and kept its sting: how {llg_he} taught, who {llg_he} broke in the teaching, and why the practice-ground at {llg_thing} is still left bare, swept every morning by someone who will not say who pays.

choices.text: Ask whom the teaching broke

effects.log: They name three, and then a fourth, ashamed to have forgotten. You carry the four names around like coins you cannot spend.

choices.text: Pretend you have a barge to catch

effects.log: You catch it. The cloud-road is exactly as long as before, and feels longer.

events.text: Cloud-children on {llg_region} are told that {llg_who} fetches the ones who linger outdoors after the lamps. The old singers know a longer version: {llg_he} reached {llg_told_age} by spending other lives, and one isle in the chain stands empty for it. You listen with a heavy stomach, and find you are checking the song for errors.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} did

effects.log: A singer tells you in half-sentences, and glances at the ceiling at the worst of it. You do not sleep.

choices.text: Say the story must be ancient by now

effects.log: It is. No one thanks you, and the singer drops the subject for a bawdier one.

events.text: A grey-haired porter on {llg_region} remembers why they do it, and tells it between mouthfuls of congee: {llg_thing} began as proof that you had settled with {llg_who}, whatever it was you owed. The gesture outlived the debt and the dread both. The porter says it lightly. His hand shakes on the bowl.

choices.text: Ask who paid the price for it

effects.log: The porter counts them off on his fingers: three names, and a place he cannot recall. The three names stay with you.

choices.text: Thank him for the congee and go

effects.log: You go. The road does not seem any shorter for being thought about.

events.text: Each spring the cloister school of {llg_region} recites the roll entry for {llg_who} aloud: dates, the age ({llg_age}), the cause ({llg_cause}), the stamp of the Jade Court. It is the dullest ritual you have ever endured. Through the wall Sirin's drum thumps out something rude. Someone worked hard, you suspect, to make this entry so dry.

choices.text: Sit through the full reading

effects.log: You are the only one who does. The master of the school gives you a nod of heartfelt thanks.

choices.text: Slip out to hear the drum

effects.log: The drum is more fun and less accurate. You come away knowing both versions, which is probably the point.

events.text: A pilgrim barge comes limping into the landing with a split keel, bound for {llg_region} to look at {llg_thing}. You hold the ropes while they re-lash it. An old woman on the afterdeck pats the planks. "You have the face for it," she says. "Come with us. It is not far."

choices.text: Step aboard

effects.log: The wind fills the sail. You are three isles along before you remember to be surprised.

choices.text: Cast off their ropes and wave

effects.log: They drift away. For days afterwards something tugs at the back of your ribs.

events.text: A trader wants a sealed packet carried to {llg_region}, with generous pay and no questions asked. You almost refuse, until you notice that you have been planning to go there anyway ever since you first heard the name {llg_thing}, and have been quietly saving for it.

choices.text: Take the packet

effects.log: The wax is warm from his hand. You sail with the evening mooring-bell.

choices.text: Suggest another courier

effects.log: Someone else takes it. You regret it mildly, for weeks, and cannot say why.

events.text: The same dream comes most nights: a stair, a hurt knee, an errand waiting at the top. You have never seen the isle in it. The dream is dull, and you wake from it every morning cross. After a year you can only think of one place it could belong, and that is {llg_region}.

choices.text: Go to {llg_region} and settle the matter

effects.log: You book passage that morning. That night, for the first time in a year, you sleep clean through.

choices.text: Take hot barley tea before bed and stay put

effects.log: It helps a little. A little is not enough, and the dream finds you again.

events.text: {llg_Thing} still stands among {llg_region}: a training terrace where the sect of {llg_who} once drilled, its flagstones worn into the shape of a stance. Sect disciples nod to you on the stairs. Your feet know where the fourth slab dips. Nobody tells you, and you do not need telling.

choices.text: Stand in the hollows and let your feet remember

effects.log: They remember, a good deal more than you do. You walk off the terrace slowly.

choices.text: Ask the doorkeeper whose terrace this was

effects.log: The doorkeeper gives a name you almost say along with him.

events.text: A house peak among {llg_region} carries the family name of {llg_who}, and the family that holds it will tell you, over tea, that the founder's ghost watches the cranes. The tea is the right kind. You know the garden path without being shown, and the keeper watches you know it.

choices.text: Admit you have the feeling of having been here

effects.log: The keeper smiles as at a familiar embarrassment. "Everyone does, the first time," comes the answer.

choices.text: Say nothing and finish the tea

effects.log: You finish it. It tastes of your own long-ago kitchen.

events.text: A shuttered pavilion hangs among the clouds of {llg_region}: {llg_thing}. Nobody will tell you why it is shut, but everyone knows. Your feet know the stair anyway, and your hand knows the bolt. You stand at the door with a coldness in the chest, as if you were the one who had to close it.

choices.text: Ask who still remembers it

effects.log: A few, it turns out. They do not like being asked, and they answer.

choices.text: Walk away from the door

effects.log: You walk. The door seems to watch you go.

events.text: The peak the cloud-pilots name {llg_thing} is empty of anything but weather. Nobody lingers there. You land in the thin air at the top and feel the old guilt of a place that was once used for something, and now is only high.

choices.text: Stay a while and see what rises in you

effects.log: It rises, slowly, and it is not pleasant. You write down some of it.

choices.text: Leave a cairn and go

effects.log: Three stones, stacked. You do not know what for.

events.text: {llg_Thing} is kept clear by common consent. Moss grows round it, not on it. The sword-immortals who pass bow stiffly and walk the long way. Your own steps take you across it before you notice, and the moss, you see, has made you a path.

choices.text: Stop in the middle and stand quiet

effects.log: The air is cold and attentive. Something decides you may leave.

choices.text: Cross it faster

effects.log: You cross. The back of your neck does not forgive you.

events.text: The Tale of {llg_who} is told on {llg_region} with the drum muffled, in a voice for secrets. It is not a long tale. Every listener leaves quieter than they came, and you know every pause in it before the teller reaches it.

choices.text: Ask the teller where the tale came from

effects.log: From those who lived it, comes the answer. That is all anyone says.

choices.text: Leave a coin and go

effects.log: The coin is taken without a word.

events.text: A custom on {llg_region} has everyone avert their eyes at a certain bend of the stair, and nobody can say why. You find your own eyes lowering before you reach it. Underneath your sleeve your wrist remembers something it should not.

choices.text: Keep your eyes up, and see what is there

effects.log: A blank wall, and a sense of being watched by it. You make yourself stay.

choices.text: Lower your eyes with the rest

effects.log: You do. It is easy, and that is what troubles you.

events.text: You have stood on this stair before; not in this body. {llg_Thing} is smaller than you remember, or you are larger, and the incense is a different kind. A young keeper looks at you, then at the lintel, then at you, with the face of someone who has just remembered a name.

choices.text: Ask the keeper what they remember

effects.log: Nothing, they say, nothing, and then, slowly, a great deal.

choices.text: Light a stick and say nothing

effects.log: The smoke rises straight. Somebody nearby breathes out.

events.text: The peak is called by another name now, but your eyes find the old line of it from far off, and your ribs ache in a way that does not belong to this body. You have been here before, in another life, and the sky has kept your shape in it.

choices.text: Fly up and look at the view

effects.log: It is the same view. It has been waiting.

choices.text: Turn back; one memory at a time

effects.log: You turn, slowly. The ache stays a day, then fades.

events.text: The terrace on {llg_region} has new flagstones laid over old, and under them, somewhere, your own footprints. You feel them through the soles. A student stops mid-form and stares, and then recovers, and bows.

choices.text: Take the stance and hold it a moment

effects.log: The stance fits like a glove worn by someone else. The student does not stop staring.

choices.text: Walk the edge, and leave it to them

effects.log: You leave it to them. They do not know what they are standing on.

events.text: A cloud-barge singer on {llg_region} is telling a tale you ought not to know the ending of, and do. You listen to the end, with the odd sense of seeing the last page of your own book. The singer looks at you across the lanterns and falters, once.

choices.text: Wait for the singer afterward

effects.log: The singer tells you the tale has a "true" version nobody can find. You nod, and say nothing.

choices.text: Slip out before the last verse

effects.log: You leave. You can hear the verse from the street.

events.text: Everyone on {llg_region} still does it the old way, and your hands join in without asking you. A woman beside you says, "You've done this before," as one remarks on the weather, and she is quite right.

choices.text: Ask her who showed her

effects.log: "The somebody of her grandmother," she says. You nod, and keep doing it.

choices.text: Keep doing it, and say nothing

effects.log: It is a comfortable silence. Your hands know more than you do.

events.text: Someone has been quietly keeping up {llg_thing} while you were away. A handrail where the steps run slick. New tiles on the north roof. A small carved mark under an eave that only one person would think to leave. The accounts show the money came in spirit stones from an unnamed donor, and you know the hand.

choices.text: Let everything stand as it is

effects.log: You do. The little mark sits where it always sat, and says nothing.

choices.text: Correct the one thing you did badly last time

effects.log: A few nails and an afternoon. It was always so small a fault.

events.text: You have stood here before. {llg_Thing} is smaller, or you larger, and the people who keep their eyes down are not the same ones, but the weight is. A cold passes through you. This is the place where you did what you did, and every stone still remembers.

choices.text: Stay and let it be heavy

effects.log: It is. You stay longer than you can bear, and a little longer.

choices.text: Leave quietly, and come back with a plan

effects.log: You leave. You will come back, you promise, and it feels like a vow.

events.text: It comes at the foot of the temple steps on a wet evening. You know how that wall was raised, for you quarrelled over its height. You know which stair creaks. {llg_name}: that was your name for {llg_age} years, until {llg_cause}, and today strangers light incense to it inside and ask it for rain.

choices.text: Take up a broom and say nothing

effects.log: You sweep the steps. The sweeping says what words would only spoil.

choices.text: Walk in and say who you were

effects.log: Heads come up. A few listen, a few laugh, and one old man covers his face.

choices.text: Seek out the keeper of the rolls and set the record straight

effects.log: The keeper writes slowly at first, then faster, then with a shaking brush.

choices.text: Pay for the repairs it was always owed

effects.log: Spirit stones go to the joiners. By the autumn the roof is sound.

events.text: You are standing on the ridge when it arrives. This was your peak. You named it from the saddle of a cloud-barge, on a morning with a cold in your head. {llg_name}: you lived {llg_age} years, died of {llg_cause}, and now the pilots call it by your title and have no idea.

choices.text: Plant a marker and tend it quietly

effects.log: A small cairn, kept clean. The cloud-pilots take it for a custom.

choices.text: Tell the next pilot who you are

effects.log: They stare, then laugh, then do not laugh.

choices.text: Go to the chart-house and correct the name

effects.log: The cartographers listen, appalled and fascinated.

choices.text: Pay for a proper beacon on the summit

effects.log: A beacon is raised by midwinter.

events.text: The sword-field is yours. You knew it the moment you set foot on it. {llg_name}: you taught here, bled here, were buried near here after {llg_age} years and a death of {llg_cause}. Students practise your stance without knowing whose it is. A boy gets it slightly wrong, and you ache to correct him.

choices.text: Take a rake and keep the field in order

effects.log: You rake until dusk. It is the best day you have had in a while.

choices.text: Show them whose stance it is

effects.log: You do the form. Nobody breathes.

choices.text: Write the true lineage down for the school

effects.log: The senior listens and takes it in, line by line.

choices.text: Pay to roof the practice hall

effects.log: The stones are paid. The rain stops coming through.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} is yours; it was sung about you. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}, and a ballad that got half of it wrong in lovely ways. You hear the singer start the third night and mouth the words, and know them better than the singer.

choices.text: Sit in the back and let it be sung

effects.log: You sit. It is strange to be moved by your own life.

choices.text: Stand up at the end and name yourself

effects.log: The singer drops the drum. The audience cannot decide.

choices.text: Take the singer aside and correct the verses

effects.log: The singer is thrilled and furious in equal measure.

choices.text: Pay for the tale to be set down on jade

effects.log: It is carved by the next spring.

events.text: The old custom of {llg_region} began with you. You know because your hands did it first, one cold morning, to keep warm. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}, and a way of doing a thing that has outlived everything else you did.

choices.text: Keep doing it, quietly, in the right way

effects.log: You do it right, and say nothing. The old people nod.

choices.text: Tell them it was yours

effects.log: Someone says "of course it was." It is not the answer you expected.

choices.text: Teach the teachers the first form

effects.log: The first form is nearly lost. You give it back.

choices.text: Pay for a hall to teach it in

effects.log: The hall is built and the doors stay open.

events.text: You are looking at the pavilion door when it comes back, all of it. You know what lies behind, since you ordered it built. You were {llg_name}. You remember the sound it made when it closed on people. {llg_age} years you lived. There are isles in this chain that bar their shutters at dusk, and they are right to.

choices.text: Find the families that remain and help where you can

effects.log: There are a few. They do not forgive you. They do let you carry water.

choices.text: Take it down yourself, starting with the roof

effects.log: You climb up and start on the beams. The isle watches without a word.

choices.text: Say aloud, to their faces, who you were

effects.log: Some turn and leave. Some stay to hear every word.

choices.text: Have it all recorded, the worst of it too

effects.log: The clerk takes a month over it. It is read once, to an empty hall, and then to a full one.

events.text: The cold hollow in the peaks is your work. You remember it now: the days leading up, the choice. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, ending in {llg_cause}, leaving behind a patch of sky no pilot will cross. You stand at its rim in the thin air, and it feels your weight.

choices.text: Seek the surviving families and make what amends you can

effects.log: There are heirs on a far isle. They accept the help, and say nothing about the rest.

choices.text: Clear away whatever still stands there

effects.log: It takes a season of work. The place is emptier, and cleaner.

choices.text: Tell the pilots plainly who you were

effects.log: The pilots fall silent. One, an old woman, gives a slow nod.

choices.text: Record all of it, including what you did

effects.log: The scribe weeps on the third page and keeps writing.

events.text: The practice-field of {llg_who} was yours. You remember what was done there. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, and {llg_cause} at the end. Moss lies thick around the border by long agreement. You cross it, and the old turf takes your footsteps as if it kept a ledger.

choices.text: Look for the families who still keep the dates

effects.log: There are a few. They let you take a spade beside them.

choices.text: Dig it over and plant it

effects.log: It takes a season. The first beans come up crooked and alive.

choices.text: Tell them who you were

effects.log: They hear it through. Nobody raises a hand against you, which is harder than a blow.

choices.text: Have the whole account written, the worst included

effects.log: The sheet fills slowly. At the foot of it, you put your name.

events.text: The dark tale of {llg_who} is yours, and the teller leaves out the worst of it, and you know the worst of it. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}. Every telling makes you a monster, and you are not sure it is wrong.

choices.text: Find who is left, and do what can be done

effects.log: A few descendants, and they know the tale well. They listen to you, warily.

choices.text: Burn every copy of the tale you can find

effects.log: You do not find them all. The attempt is its own confession.

choices.text: Tell them to their faces who you were

effects.log: The teller stops, lowers the drum. A silence follows.

choices.text: Get the whole of it written down, the worst included

effects.log: It is written. It is long. It is true.

events.text: The dark custom began with your word. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death by {llg_cause}. They turn their faces at the bend in the stair, and do not know why they do it. You do.

choices.text: Find the people it harmed and listen to them

effects.log: They are scattered, but a few come. You hear all of them out, and take no notes.

choices.text: End the custom, aloud, in front of them

effects.log: You say it plainly where they all gather. It fades slowly, then very suddenly.

choices.text: Tell them who began it

effects.log: They stare. The custom falters in front of you.

choices.text: Have the whole history written down

effects.log: The first page is the hardest. After that it goes quicker.

events.text: You tend {llg_thing} as it should be tended. Nobody asks who you are. The lamps are trimmed, the stair swept, the incense kept dry. Slowly the pilgrims notice that someone has been careful with the place. An old nun leaves a gift of tea at the door every dawn, and does not wait to be thanked.

choices.text: Keep it up, year on year

effects.log: The tea comes every dawn. The temple glows quietly.

choices.text: Teach a young keeper the work

effects.log: The keeper learns fast. You step back, content.

events.text: You tend the peak: clear the cairns, mend the guide-rope, keep the beacon lit on stormy nights. Pilots begin to leave a tithe of cloud-silk at the top. They do not know why. They do know the place feels kept.

choices.text: Keep the beacon fed

effects.log: It burns through the long winter. The pilots speak of a good spirit on the peak.

choices.text: Plant something hardy at the top

effects.log: A twisted pine takes root. The wind has opinions.

events.text: You tend what was left, in the way that needs no name: the school's old terrace, the telling at the quay, the way of doing a thing. You do it without credit. Everyone assumes it was always like this, which is the highest praise you could have asked.

choices.text: Keep doing it without a word

effects.log: No one thanks you. The thing goes on.

choices.text: Let one person in on it

effects.log: A young person learns what you do and why. It will outlast you.

events.text: You tend the dark thing as one tends a grave: carefully, daily, without ceremony. The isle watches, uncertain whether this is penance or presumption. After a season someone leaves a lantern at the gate. After a year, two lanterns.

choices.text: Keep going, however slowly it is forgiven

effects.log: It is not forgiven. It is accepted, which is something else.

choices.text: Ask a survivor what they need

effects.log: The answer is small and simple. You provide it.

events.text: You tell them. Some of the old folk here had grandparents who knew someone who knew {llg_who}, and they keep a test for claimants, since you are far from the first: three questions. What did {llg_he} eat at dawn? Whom did {llg_he} never forgive? What carried {llg_he} off? An old woman cups her ear. No claimant has ever got all three.

choices.text: Answer in the way only you could

ok.log: You answer all three. The old woman sits back slowly. The crowd murmurs, and one by one they bow.

fail.log: You stumble on the second. They smile politely, and the old woman shakes her head.

choices.text: Offer them a sample of the old skill

ok.log: The challenger goes down. The stance is exactly the one in the old woodcut.

fail.log: The challenger is quicker than the woodcut implied. You go down, and the doubters nod.

choices.text: Laugh, and say it was a joke

effects.log: You laugh and call it nonsense. Some are relieved. A few are not.

events.text: You told them. The grandparents' tales have grown on {llg_region}, and your plain account sounds small beside them. Someone has a test ready: three questions, set by a long-dead abbot. What did {llg_he} drink at dawn? Whom did {llg_he} never forgive? What carried {llg_he} off? The whole terrace falls quiet.

choices.text: Answer as only you could

ok.log: You answer all three, with a detail that makes someone gasp. The terrace bows, awkwardly.

fail.log: The soup is wrong, apparently. Polite smiles, and a long silence.

choices.text: Offer them a sample of the old skill

ok.log: The challenger drops. The old form, done exactly. Someone starts to cry.

fail.log: You were stronger once. The challenger is gracious about it, which is worse.

choices.text: Laugh, and take it back

effects.log: You laugh and say it was a joke. Some are relieved. A few are not.

events.text: You told them. By now {llg_who} is a myth on {llg_region}, and a stranger saying "I was {llg_he}" is a joke the cloud-barges have heard before. A solemn old priest of the myth sets you three questions in a dead dialect. The whole quay watches.

choices.text: Answer as only you could

ok.log: You answer in the dead dialect, correctly. The priest takes off his hat. The quay does not know whether to cheer.

fail.log: Wrong on the second. The priest pats your arm kindly, as for a child.

choices.text: Offer them a sample of the old skill

ok.log: The challenger yields. The form is older than the dialect.

fail.log: You are knocked flat. Nobody believes a legend can lose, so nobody believes you.

choices.text: Laugh, and take it back

effects.log: You laugh and say it was a joke. A few cloud-sprites cheer.

events.text: You told them who you were. No one forgave anything. They listened as if you were a verdict. Some stood to leave, then did not. The silence afterward was the longest of your lives.

choices.text: Stand there and take whatever comes

effects.log: What comes is quiet and harsh. You stand through it.

choices.text: Offer to go, and stay if they say stay

effects.log: They do not say go. They do not say stay. You stay.

events.text: Archivist Eun Haru of the Jade Court's rolls has ink on her cuffs and no time to spare. For nineteen years she has been working on the faults in the entry for {llg_who}. "Three of my predecessors lost their minds," she says, writing. Then she reads your list, and stops. "How do you know the colour of the shutters?" You had written nothing about shutters.

choices.text: Tell her it was handed down to you

effects.log: She narrows her eyes, and finally accepts it as a source, with visible reluctance.

choices.text: Tell her the truth and see what she does

effects.log: The brush goes down. "I suspected something of the kind," she says. The entry is amended before the lamps are lit.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} has grown wrong in a hundred ways, and a few right ones. You go from barge to barge correcting small things, patiently: the date, the ending, the soup. A singer resists, then relents. "It is a worse tale," the singer says, "and truer. I will sing the true one at the quay."

choices.text: Give the singer the true verses, one by one

effects.log: The singer writes them down. The quay notices the change by autumn.

choices.text: Leave the singer to decide

effects.log: The singer sings the false one, with a pause where the true one used to be.

events.text: You have the whole of it written down, the worst included. The Jade Court's archivist reads it twice, and asks if you want it entered under your own name. You do not. It is entered under a number, and any scholar may find it who looks.

choices.text: Sign it, in the end, with your old name

effects.log: The old name still suits the pen. You wonder at that.

choices.text: Leave it unsigned

effects.log: It is read. It is cited. Nobody knows whose it is.

events.text: The work goes on all year: the drain they ought to have dug, the broken step, the roof. The chief carpenter asks whose money this is. Nobody's, you say. He looks at your drawings, then at the old wall, then at you. "Same hand," he mutters, and decides it is not his business. The temple holds a dinner for the unnamed donor. You are placed at the end of the table.

choices.text: Go to the dinner and eat heartily

effects.log: You eat well. They toast the donor, and you raise your teacup to the toast. It is oddly comfortable.

choices.text: Scratch a small mark on a beam where only you would think to look

effects.log: One tiny glyph, high under a rafter. A hundred years on, you will find it again.

events.text: A beacon-tower goes up on the peak that year, paid by an anonymous patron, built by a crew who ask no questions. On the first clear night the tower lights, and the pilots of {llg_region} swing round to look. The old keeper says it is the best fire he has seen. You say nothing.

choices.text: Watch it light, and watch the pilots

effects.log: Their faces are the gift. You take it home.

choices.text: Hang a small lantern of your own beside it

effects.log: A tiny flame next to the great one. It outlasts the winter.

events.text: A roofed hall goes up beside the old terrace: a place to rest between forms, and to practise out of the rain. The sword-immortals who use it give the donor a nickname, "the Dry One." You smile, and let them.

choices.text: Sit in it on a rainy day, among strangers

effects.log: The rain on the roof is the best sound. Nobody guesses.

choices.text: Add a small stove, quietly

effects.log: The stove warms the winter forms. A mystery grows round it.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} is set down in jade, cut by a family of carvers, and hung in the harbour hall of {llg_region}. It is not the whole tale. But the plaque will outlast the singers, and the true line is on it: the one nobody believes and everybody keeps.

choices.text: Stand in the hall and let the singers come

effects.log: They come. Some read, some sing. You are the quietest listener.

choices.text: Pay the carvers an extra, secretly

effects.log: The carvers add a border of cranes. Nobody asks who asked for it.

events.text: A schoolhouse for the custom goes up on {llg_region}, teaching the way to anyone who asks. It opens with nine pupils and no explanation. By spring it has forty, and a waiting list. The founder's name is not on it, which suits you perfectly.

choices.text: Watch the first lesson from the back

effects.log: The teacher stumbles once, recovers. You nod, silently.

choices.text: Leave your best manual on the shelf

effects.log: It is found within the month, and used.

events.text: It took a season to raise and takes nine to pull down. No one helps at first. Then one morning a boy from the isle with the barred shutters climbs up and lifts a stone, asking nothing. His father follows. They never speak to you. When the last of the wall is gone, the entire isle comes up to stand in the open air where it used to be.

choices.text: Stand with them and look at the empty place

effects.log: You stand. Nobody speaks. It is the quietest and most useful hour of your life.

choices.text: Slip away before they arrive

effects.log: You are gone by dawn. The isle will wonder, for a long time, who did it.

events.text: You begin by taking the name off the map. It is easier than you expected: a few cartographers were already uneasy. The pilots of {llg_region} watch the new line go in, and begin to fly across the old gap again. The weather is merely weather.

choices.text: Fly across it yourself, once, slowly

effects.log: It is only sky. The sky does not forgive, but it does not hold on.

choices.text: Leave a quiet marker at the edge

effects.log: A small stone with a number on it. Pilots leave it alone.

events.text: You undo what can be undone, piece by piece: the custom, the tale, the sealed hall. It is slow, unglamorous work, and it makes you no friends. But a day comes when a child asks about the old thing and no one knows what to say, and you feel a long breath go out of the world.

choices.text: Tell the child the plain truth, kindly

effects.log: The child listens, nods, and goes to play. That is all anyone wanted.

choices.text: Let the question lapse

effects.log: It lapses. It will not be missed.

events.text: An old woman named Tobeom comes up the stairs one autumn with a pack and a walking-pole. She tends old places, she says, from isle to isle, because someone ought to and nobody pays. She looks over your work on {llg_thing}, clicks her tongue, and hands you the end of a rope. You hold it. An hour on, you are halfway up the scaffold yourself.

choices.text: Ask what she counts as an old place

effects.log: She names about forty. Most lie under cloud, now. You are on her list.

choices.text: Keep holding the rope

effects.log: She works, you steady. Small talk drifts up and down the scaffold.

events.text: Old Tobeom comes by again, with her young apprentice, Mirae. She inspects the work in silence, runs a thumb across a joint and does not criticise it, which from her is a kind of speech. Mirae tells you in a whisper that Tobeom has never been seen to eat.

choices.text: Offer them both a hot meal

effects.log: Tobeom eats a small bowl, to the astonishment of Mirae. You are, quietly, adopted.

choices.text: Ask Mirae how she came to this

effects.log: A short story. A long respect. You will hear the rest later.

events.text: Tobeom arrives to find the roof of a half-forgotten shrine collapsed. She does not rage. She sits and looks at it for an hour, then begins to sort the beams. Mirae, grimly cheerful, hands you a mallet. "This is how it always begins," she says.

choices.text: Take the mallet and begin

effects.log: It is two weeks of work and an unreasonable amount of tea. The roof goes up.

choices.text: Sit with Tobeom and say nothing

effects.log: You sit. Something about the silence is helpful.

events.text: A rich young patron arrives to inspect {llg_thing} with a retinue, a poet and a plan to have it gilded. His permits are in order. Tobeom plants herself before him with her pole and is walked around. He asks you, whom he takes for the foreman, where the gilders should start. A pendant at his throat bears the name of {llg_who}.

choices.text: Point him to the real rot and let his silver go there

effects.log: He is more embarrassed than offended. The silver goes to the right beams, and the pendant stays on.

choices.text: Gently talk him out of the gilding

ok.log: You walk him through the whole place. By the end he is carrying a bucket. Tobeom pats your arm in passing.

fail.log: He will not be moved. The gilders start on the wrong wall, and Tobeom sighs for a week.

events.text: Tobeom is old now. She sits on the step of {llg_thing} and watches Mirae hammering, and tells you, unprompted, what she would like done with her tools when she goes. You take notes. She watches you do it and says, "You are going to be better at this than I was." It is not a compliment. It is a handover.

choices.text: Promise to keep the tools in use

effects.log: The promise is easy. Keeping it will take the rest of your life.

choices.text: Say she has years left yet

effects.log: She snorts. She does not have, and you both know it.

events.text: A broad islander with a ferryman's hands arrives at your door: Rho Danbi. His family has kept an account for five generations, and he wants to read it out to whoever now looks after {llg_thing}, being the nearest thing to the responsible party. He sits and reads for three hours. Names and years, and nothing else. He never lifts his voice.

choices.text: Listen to the end and ask him for a copy

effects.log: He hands it over. The paper is soft as cloth with handling. You keep it.

choices.text: Remark that all this was a very long time ago

effects.log: He regards you for a long moment. "Yes," he says. "That is what we all say, in the end." He leaves.

events.text: Rho Danbi has pieced it together, or enough of it. Nobody ever learns how. He climbs the stair at dusk with a boat-hook in one hand, unhurried, and says he is not a fool and does not know how such things can be, but his grandmother told him what to look for. He says your hands are the same hands. He has come far. He lays the hook down between you.

choices.text: Kneel and leave the hook where it lies

effects.log: He looks at you a long while. Then he takes the hook and goes down the stair. It is not forgiveness. It is a beginning.

choices.text: Tell him what you have made of this life, and let him judge

ok.log: He hears all of it. He weighs it. He nods once and takes up the hook.

fail.log: He weighs it, and finds it light, and leaves the hook behind, which is a small mercy.

events.text: Rho Danbi sends word that his daughter will carry the reckoning from now on. He is tired, he says, and the book is heavy. A small girl with serious eyes appears at the gate with a satchel, and asks if she may read you the first name. She reads it clearly. She has been practising.

choices.text: Listen to all the names, however long it takes

effects.log: It takes an afternoon. She does not hurry, and neither do you.

choices.text: Ask her to read slowly, so you can remember them

effects.log: She slows. By dusk you can say a dozen of them yourself.

events.text: The reckoning has been carried to the last of the family, an old woman who writes poorly and reads with a finger. She brings you a gift: a spare copy, so that two houses hold it. You understand the gesture. It is a trust, or a sentence, or both. You take it in both hands.

choices.text: Promise to keep it where the next generation can find it

effects.log: You promise, and keep it, and the next generation does find it.

choices.text: Offer to add your own page at the end

effects.log: She nods, and gives you a pen. You write for an hour.

events.text: You have grown old tending {llg_thing}. The isle has adopted you as a fixture; schoolchildren wave. At the evening tea an old pilgrim asks if the place is quiet. "It is," you say, and look at the stair, and for a moment know every foot that ever climbed it. The tea is hot. The air is clean.

choices.text: Sit a while longer

effects.log: The light turns gold. Somebody is sweeping, far off.

choices.text: Say good evening to the stair

effects.log: The stair does not answer. You do not mind.

events.text: Late in life you are still being asked to prove it, now and again, by cheerful young scholars with notebooks. You do. Sometimes they believe you. Sometimes they say "how marvellous" and write down something else. It no longer troubles you. The place knows. That is enough.

choices.text: Answer one more question, graciously

effects.log: You answer. The scholar writes it down, half-believing.

choices.text: Close the door gently on the notebook

effects.log: You close it. The lamp on the table is warm.

events.text: Your corrections have become the standard entry. The Jade Court's rolls now carry them, and children learn the true dates. You pass through the records office once a year on pilgrimage. Nobody there knows you; the clerk bows at the door, and that is all it takes.

choices.text: Leave a small note on the desk of the clerk

effects.log: The note says only thanks. The clerk will puzzle over it for a week.

choices.text: Walk out into the evening

effects.log: The evening is mild. The rolls are right, and that is quietly enough.

events.text: The hall you built still stands, a little weathered. Children play on its steps, ignorant of whoever paid for it. The roof does not leak. You watch from across the lane with a cup of tea, and the roof is the best thing you ever did.

choices.text: Pay for the next repair, quietly

effects.log: It is done by someone who does not ask. The roof holds.

choices.text: Watch the children

effects.log: They run in and out of the rain. You smile like a fool.

events.text: You tried to atone, and the ages have worn on, and the work is not finished, and never will be. A younger person has taken up the broom. You tell them what you know. They write it down, and do not ask for more, and that is all you can ask.

choices.text: Hand over the broom

effects.log: It is lighter than you remembered. The younger one holds it with care.

choices.text: Keep sweeping, since you can still

effects.log: You sweep a little each morning. The stair is cleaner for it.

events.text: It is gone, the thing you tore down. Where it stood is a garden now, and a cloud of bees, and a little plaque nobody reads. You visit on warm days. The air is clear. You do not forgive yourself, but you have stopped waiting for the day you would.

choices.text: Sit among the bees

effects.log: They tolerate you. You doze a little.

choices.text: Pull a weed or two

effects.log: A small job, and good. The garden is yours to weed, if not to own.

events.text: You have not visited in years. It still stands, you hear: {llg_thing}, in {llg_region}. Only last week at the quay a stranger told it wrongly, and you let it pass. Then you paid for the whole table without explaining, and walked out into the chill feeling lighter than you had any right to feel.

choices.text: Walk home the long way round

effects.log: The long way is longer than you remember. It is worth every step.

choices.text: Go back inside and hear how it ends

effects.log: The ending is worse than you feared, and better told.

events.text: Chuyeol the pilgrim climbs onto an offering-crate each noon and rattles a gourd until someone listens. Today it is {llg_who}, who reached {llg_told_age} and left {llg_thing} in {llg_region}. "My mother swept its floors," Chuyeol says, "and she was a hard woman to impress." The telling is plain and a little shy. You find you have missed your own appointment.

choices.text: Ask Chuyeol which court it stands in

effects.log: Chuyeol names the court and wants a small coin for the naming. You pay, and the way lodges itself in your memory.

choices.text: Drop a coin in the gourd and move on

effects.log: The gourd gives a thankful rattle. The name goes with you, like a stone in the lining of a robe.

events.text: "And when {llg_who} came to {llg_region}, the heavens themselves bowed," shouts Chuyeol, arms wide. "So they raised {llg_thing} where the heavens bowed. {llg_He} lived {llg_told_age} ages and never once sat down." You think no one could be so foolish, and are annoyed, and cannot say why.

choices.text: Say that no one could live that way

effects.log: "You have seen it, have you?" Chuyeol grins, and the steps laugh. For a moment you feel you have.

choices.text: Ask what the faithful ask of the hall these days

effects.log: Rain, harvests, sons, says Chuyeol. Most go unanswered. They go on asking.

events.text: The festival route-sheets list a pilgrim's hill that was nameless last season: {llg_thing}, after {llg_who}. The woman selling them says {llg_he} died of {llg_cause}, or so her mother told her, and she crosses two fingers over the stack. The name goes into you sideways. You ask her to read it out again.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} was like

effects.log: "Restless," she says. "Or very still. I forget which." You laugh, and are astonished at how glad it makes you.

choices.text: Press the name into the wax of your seal-ring

effects.log: The wax goes soft in the first warm month. By then the name has long since set in you.

events.text: Junior deities in {llg_region} learn the high places by a chanting-game, and {llg_Thing} is always the third name in the chain. A temple cook, asked what it means, says it was a word for some vast creature from before the first altar. The explanation is confident and obviously borrowed. Something in you says that is wrong, softly, as if remembering a taste.

choices.text: Chant the game again until the word stops being a word

effects.log: The word breaks into sounds, and a fraction of a meaning slips out between them. You hold on to that.

choices.text: Rejoin the chanting and stumble at the third name

effects.log: Your voice trips on it, every time. The younger deities find it unbearably funny.

events.text: An aged war-god at the stall leans on a crutch and tells how he learned his first stances at {llg_thing} in {llg_region}, from a teacher who had it from one who had it from {llg_who}, {llg_years} years back. "Hollows in the stone," he says, "for the heels." Your own heels are already set, apart, as if the stone were under them.

choices.text: Ask him to demonstrate the stance

effects.log: He demonstrates it with a wince, gets it wrong, and corrects it. You see the error before he does, and neither of you knows why.

choices.text: Fill his cup again and settle in

effects.log: He wanders through half a century of drill-yard talk. The hollows come up in every version of the tale.

events.text: Priests of the martial pantheons teach that every fighting art was born at {llg_thing} in {llg_region}, on the day a god of battles lost an argument to a mountain. {llg_who} is the name on that god. The Heavenly Court keeps six shelves of exegesis. The festival stalls sell a honey-cake in the shape of the loser.

choices.text: Buy a honey-cake

effects.log: The cake figure stands in a stance that is wrong at the feet. You eat it, thinking about the feet, and cannot say how you know.

choices.text: Ask who taught the god of battles

effects.log: The stallholder shakes with laughter and sits on an upturned bowl. You asked in earnest, and feel it.

events.text: A processional hymn has taken the exchange by storm, "{llg_song}", and the refrain goes "{llg_verse}". It praises {llg_who}, gone at {llg_told_age} of {llg_cause}, as the singer insists. You have never heard a note of it. The next line rises in your head before she reaches it, and hers is wrong, and you wince openly.

choices.text: Sing your next line under hers

effects.log: She falters and stares at you. "Who taught you that?" You cannot say, and she presses a sesame cake into your hand.

choices.text: Pay the choir a coin and keep quiet

effects.log: It is a good hymn. You hum it for a week, and it improves your temper.

events.text: The Passion of {llg_who} now runs three evenings at the pilgrim theatre. On the first, {llg_he} turns back a flood. On the second {llg_he} is wed, by troupe, to a spirit of the river or a heron. On the third {llg_he} dies of {llg_cause} at {llg_told_age} and the house weeps in unison. You weep as well, and judge the play silly.

choices.text: Return for the second and third evenings

effects.log: The week is gone before you know it. The heron is the best of it. You recall no heron, and feel a small, odd loss.

choices.text: Ask the prompter what is true in it

effects.log: "All of it," she whispers, "by now." You mull that for a long time, and decide she is right.

events.text: In {llg_region} they begin every rite with the same small gesture and have for {llg_years} years: palm to heart, then a single bow of the head, then the first word. A temple child says that is simply how it begins. Nobody can say who began it. You stand watching, and find your palm already on your chest.

choices.text: Ask the child to teach it properly

effects.log: She does, gravely, and you carry it through better than she can. She concludes you studied there, and you let her think so.

choices.text: Drop your hand and walk on

effects.log: You do. For a week your palm keeps drifting back to your chest, and you keep sending it down.

events.text: The custom in {llg_region} is so woven into the day that nobody calls it a custom, as no one calls breathing a habit. Scholars of the Court trace it to the first dawn. None suggests that any being began it. You do it yourself, unthinking, in a gateway, and you have never been within an age of the place.

choices.text: Do it on purpose and notice how it feels

effects.log: It feels entirely right, which seems unfair. You walk around cheerful and baffled for the rest of the day.

choices.text: Fold your hands and think about supper

effects.log: You think about supper. Your hands, folded, are still doing it.

events.text: After the evening gong nobody in {llg_region} says the name {llg_who}. Chuyeol will, for twice the usual coin, with a hand cupped to the mouth: how {llg_he} closed a fist on the courts, how {llg_thing} was shuttered, and how it has stayed that way for {llg_years} years because no one wants to learn what answers if it is opened. Your mouth dries. You pay.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} did

effects.log: Chuyeol gives you a short, dreadful account. You rest badly for a week, and the name sounds more and more like yours.

choices.text: Say it was a very long time ago

effects.log: It was. Nobody thanks you for saying so, and you leave the stall faster than manners allow.

events.text: The pilgrim guides mark a barren rise in {llg_region} as {llg_thing} and warn walkers to go round. They say {llg_who} did something there, {llg_years} years ago or more, to the beings living below it. No guide will tell you what. They study their sandals as they don't tell you, and so do you.

choices.text: Ask the guide what {llg_he} did

effects.log: One of them says a few halting words, stops at the worst, and looks away. You rest badly for nights, and cannot say why it feels familiar.

choices.text: Observe that it was ages ago

effects.log: It was. The guide falls silent, and you take the lower road, quicker than courtesy permits.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} among the war-gods is all sting and no thunder: where {llg_he} trained pupils, what {llg_he} did to the ones who failed, and why the yard at {llg_thing} is kept swept and empty by a caretaker who will not say who pays.

choices.text: Ask who suffered under it

effects.log: They list three, then a fourth with a catch in the voice. You carry the names around like coins you cannot spend.

choices.text: Mention a meeting you need to reach

effects.log: You reach it. The road is the same length as ever, and feels longer.

events.text: Little gods in {llg_region} are warned that {llg_who} collects those who dawdle outside after the evening gong. The old chanters keep a darker version: {llg_he} lived to {llg_told_age} by spending the ages of lesser deities, and a shrine somewhere stands unlit for it. You listen with a leaden stomach, and catch yourself testing the verses for slips.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} did

effects.log: A chanter tells you in broken lines, watching the lamp at the worst of it. You do not rest.

choices.text: Say the tale must be older than the temple

effects.log: It is. No one thanks you, and the chanter moves on to a rowdier tune.

events.text: An elderly door-keeper in {llg_region} remembers the point of it, and offers it between sips of broth: {llg_thing} was first a way to prove you had paid up with {llg_who}, whatever the debt had been. The gesture outlasted both the debt and the dread. The door-keeper says it lightly, and the bowl trembles in his hands.

choices.text: Ask who paid for it

effects.log: He counts them on his fingers: three names, and a place he cannot recall. The three names stay with you.

choices.text: Thank him for the broth and leave

effects.log: You leave. The road is no shorter for having been thought about.

events.text: Every year the temple school of {llg_region} chants the register entry on {llg_who}: dates, the age ({llg_age}), the cause ({llg_cause}), the seal of the Court. It is the driest rite you have ever sat through. Beyond the wall Chuyeol's gourd rattles out something rude. Someone, you decide, went to real trouble to make this entry boring.

choices.text: Sit through the whole chant

effects.log: You are the only one who does. The headmistress gives you a nod of heartfelt thanks.

choices.text: Slip out to the rattle

effects.log: The rattle is livelier and less accurate. You come away with both versions, which is likely the idea.

events.text: A pilgrim cloud-boat drifts in with a cracked keel, bound for {llg_region} to see {llg_thing}. You help lift the repair-plank. An old priestess on the stern pats the bench beside her. "You have the look," she says. "Come along. It is only a few seasons."

choices.text: Climb aboard

effects.log: The boat catches the wind. You are on the way before you have decided to go.

choices.text: Wave them off

effects.log: They drift out of sight. You feel the pull for days.

events.text: A temple steward wants a sealed tablet delivered to {llg_region}, generous offering, no questions. You are on the point of refusing when you realise you had planned to go there anyway, ever since you heard the name {llg_thing}, and have been quietly setting aside the time.

choices.text: Take the tablet

effects.log: The seal is warm from the steward's hand. You set out with the evening procession.

choices.text: Suggest another bearer

effects.log: Someone else takes it. You regret it faintly, for ages, and cannot say why.

events.text: Most nights the same dream returns: a stair, a bad knee, an errand waiting at the top. You have never seen the court in it. The dream is dull, yet you wake from it cross each morning. After a year you can think of only one place it fits, and that is {llg_region}.

choices.text: Go to {llg_region} and put it to rest

effects.log: You leave that morning. That night, for the first time in a year, you sleep right through.

choices.text: Warm a cup of milk before sleeping and stay put

effects.log: It helps a little. A little does not suffice, and the dream finds you again.

events.text: A great temple of your own domain stands in {llg_region}: {llg_Thing}, raised in the name of {llg_who}. Worshippers climb its steps on festival days. The offering-bowls are of a pattern you would have chosen. The priest at the door looks at you, then at the lintel, then at you, as if waiting to be told.

choices.text: Light a stick and stand where the faithful stand

effects.log: The smoke rises straight. The priest breathes out.

choices.text: Ask the priest how long it has stood

effects.log: They give a number of years, and a story. The story is nearly right.

events.text: Your pantheon's hymns have a verse you did not teach them. It tells of {llg_who} and the founding of a council, and it is sung at the great feasts of {llg_region}. You know the next line before the choir reaches it, and you know it is slightly wrong.

choices.text: Sing the right line, quietly

effects.log: The choir stumbles, then rights itself. A young priest looks round.

choices.text: Listen to the end and say nothing

effects.log: The hymn finishes. The silence afterward is warm.

events.text: A sealed shrine stands in {llg_region}: {llg_thing}. Nobody will tell you why it is shut, but everyone knows. Your feet know the steps anyway, and your hand knows the bolt. You stand at the door with a coldness in the chest, as if you were the one who had to close it.

choices.text: Ask who still remembers it

effects.log: A few, it turns out. They do not like being asked, and they answer.

choices.text: Walk away from the door

effects.log: You walk. The door seems to watch you go.

events.text: The height the pilgrims call {llg_thing} is empty of anything but weather. Nobody lingers there. You land in the thin air at the top and feel the old guilt of a place once used for something, and now only high.

choices.text: Stay a while and see what rises in you

effects.log: It rises, slowly, and it is not pleasant. You write down some of it.

choices.text: Leave a cairn and go

effects.log: Three stones, stacked. You do not know what for.

events.text: {llg_Thing} is kept clear by common consent. Moss grows round it, not on it. War-gods who pass bow stiffly and walk the long way. Your own steps take you across it before you notice, and the moss, you see, has made you a path.

choices.text: Stop in the middle and stand quiet

effects.log: The air is cold and attentive. Something decides you may leave.

choices.text: Cross it faster

effects.log: You cross. The back of your neck does not forgive you.

events.text: The Tale of {llg_who} is told in {llg_region} with the rattle muffled, in a voice for secrets. It is not a long tale. Every listener leaves quieter than they came, and you know every pause in it before the teller reaches it.

choices.text: Ask the teller where the tale came from

effects.log: From those who lived it, comes the answer. That is all anyone says.

choices.text: Leave a coin and go

effects.log: The coin is taken without a word.

events.text: A custom in {llg_region} has everyone avert their eyes at a certain bend of the temple stair, and nobody can say why. You find your own eyes lowering before you reach it. Underneath your sleeve your wrist remembers something it should not.

choices.text: Keep your eyes up, and see what is there

effects.log: A blank wall, and a sense of being watched by it. You make yourself stay.

choices.text: Lower your eyes with the rest

effects.log: You do. It is easy, and that is what troubles you.

events.text: You have stood on this step before; not in this form. {llg_Thing} is smaller than you remember, or you are larger, and the incense is a different kind. A young priest looks at you, then at the lintel, then at you, with the face of someone who has just remembered a name.

choices.text: Ask the priest what they remember

effects.log: Nothing, they say, nothing, and then, slowly, a great deal.

choices.text: Light a stick and say nothing

effects.log: The smoke rises straight. Somebody nearby breathes out.

events.text: The height is called by another name now, but your eyes find the old line of it from far off, and your ribs ache in a way that does not belong to this form. You have been here before, in another life, and the sky has kept your shape in it.

choices.text: Rise and look at the view

effects.log: It is the same view. It has been waiting.

choices.text: Turn back; one memory at a time

effects.log: You turn, slowly. The ache stays a day, then fades.

events.text: The court in {llg_region} has new flagstones laid over old, and under them, somewhere, your own footprints. You feel them through the soles. A young war-god stops mid-form and stares, and then recovers, and bows.

choices.text: Take the stance and hold it a moment

effects.log: The stance fits like a glove worn by someone else. The young god does not stop staring.

choices.text: Walk the edge, and leave it to them

effects.log: You leave it to them. They do not know what they are standing on.

events.text: A pilgrim in {llg_region} is telling a tale you ought not to know the ending of, and do. You listen to the end, with the odd sense of seeing the last page of your own book. The pilgrim looks at you across the lamps and falters, once.

choices.text: Wait for the pilgrim afterward

effects.log: The pilgrim says the tale has a "true" version nobody can find. You nod, and say nothing.

choices.text: Slip out before the last verse

effects.log: You leave. You can hear the verse from the street.

events.text: Everyone in {llg_region} still does it the old way, and your hands join in without asking you. A priestess beside you says, "You have done this before," as one remarks on the weather, and she is quite right.

choices.text: Ask her who showed her

effects.log: The somebody of her grandmother, she says. You nod, and keep doing it.

choices.text: Keep doing it, and say nothing

effects.log: It is a comfortable silence. Your hands know more than you do.

events.text: Someone has quietly kept {llg_thing} in repair while you were gone. A rail by the slippery steps. New tiles on the north roof. A tiny carved mark under an eave that only one hand would leave. The accounts say the faith came in from an unnamed donor, and you know the hand.

choices.text: Let everything stand

effects.log: You do. The little mark sits where it has always sat, and says nothing.

choices.text: Correct the one thing you did badly the first time

effects.log: A few nails and an afternoon. It was always so small a fault.

events.text: You have stood here before. {llg_Thing} is smaller, or you larger, and the beings who keep their eyes down are not the same ones, but the weight is. A cold passes through you. This is the place where you did what you did, and every stone still remembers.

choices.text: Stay and let it be heavy

effects.log: It is. You stay longer than you can bear, and a little longer.

choices.text: Leave quietly, and come back with a plan

effects.log: You leave. You will come back, you promise, and it feels like a vow.

events.text: It comes upon you at the temple stair on a wet evening, all of it at once. You know how that wall was raised, since you fought over its height. You know which stair creaks. {llg_name}: that was you, for {llg_age} years, until {llg_cause}, and now strangers burn incense to the name inside and ask it for rain.

choices.text: Take up a broom and say nothing

effects.log: You sweep the steps. The sweeping says what words would only spoil.

choices.text: Walk in and say who you were

effects.log: Heads come up. A few listen, a few laugh, and an old priest covers his face.

choices.text: Seek the keeper of the Book and set the record straight

effects.log: The keeper writes slowly at first, then faster, then with a shaking quill.

choices.text: Give it what it was always owed

effects.log: Offerings go to the masons. By the autumn the roof is sound.

events.text: You are standing on the height when it arrives. This was your peak. You named it from a cloud-saddle, on a morning with a cold in your head. {llg_name}: you lived {llg_age} years, died of {llg_cause}, and now the pilgrims call it by your title and have no idea.

choices.text: Plant a marker and tend it quietly

effects.log: A small cairn, kept clean. The pilgrims take it for a custom.

choices.text: Tell the next pilgrim who you are

effects.log: They stare, then laugh, then do not laugh.

choices.text: Go to the map-hall and correct the name

effects.log: The mapmakers listen, appalled and fascinated.

choices.text: Give for a proper beacon on the summit

effects.log: A beacon is raised by midwinter.

events.text: The drill-court is yours. You knew it the moment you set foot on it. {llg_name}: you taught here, bled here, were laid to rest near here after {llg_age} years and a death of {llg_cause}. Pupils practise your stance without knowing whose it is. A boy gets it slightly wrong, and you ache to correct him.

choices.text: Take a rake and keep the court in order

effects.log: You rake until dusk. It is the best day you have had in a while.

choices.text: Show them whose stance it is

effects.log: You do the form. Nobody breathes.

choices.text: Write the true lineage down for the school

effects.log: The senior listens and takes it in, line by line.

choices.text: Give to roof the practice hall

effects.log: The offerings are made. The rain stops coming through.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} is yours; it was sung about you. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}, and a hymn that got half of it wrong in lovely ways. You hear the pilgrim start the third night and mouth the words, and know them better than the pilgrim.

choices.text: Sit at the back and let it be sung

effects.log: You sit. It is strange to be moved by your own life.

choices.text: Stand up at the end and name yourself

effects.log: The pilgrim drops the rattle. The audience cannot decide.

choices.text: Take the pilgrim aside and correct the verses

effects.log: The pilgrim is thrilled and furious in equal measure.

choices.text: Give for the tale to be set down on a tablet

effects.log: It is carved by the next spring.

events.text: The ancient practice of {llg_region} started with you. Your hands performed it first, on a bitter dawn, for warmth. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}, and a little gesture that has outlasted every grander thing you ever did.

choices.text: Keep doing it, quietly, in the right way

effects.log: You do it right, and say nothing. The old priests nod.

choices.text: Tell them it was yours

effects.log: Someone says "of course it was." It is not the answer you expected.

choices.text: Teach the teachers the first form

effects.log: The first form is nearly lost. You give it back.

choices.text: Give for a hall to teach it in

effects.log: The hall is built and the doors stay open.

events.text: You are looking at the shrine door when it comes back to you. You know what lies behind it, since you had it built. You were {llg_name}. You remember the sound it made when it shut on living beings. {llg_age} years you held it. There are courts along this road that bar their doors at dusk, and they are right to.

choices.text: Find the families that remain and help where you can

effects.log: There are a few. They do not forgive you. They do let you carry water.

choices.text: Take it down yourself, starting with the roof

effects.log: You climb up and begin on the beams. The court watches without a word.

choices.text: Say aloud, to their faces, who you were

effects.log: Some turn and leave. Some stay to hear every word.

choices.text: Have it all recorded, the worst of it too

effects.log: The scribes take a season. It is read once, to an empty hall, and then to a full one.

events.text: The barren rise is your work. It returns to you now: the days before it, the choice. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, ending in {llg_cause}, leaving a hill no pilgrim will climb. You stand at its rim in the thin air, and it feels your weight.

choices.text: Seek the surviving families and make what amends you can

effects.log: There are heirs in a far court. They accept the help, and say nothing about the rest.

choices.text: Clear away whatever still stands there

effects.log: It takes a season of work. The place is emptier, and cleaner.

choices.text: Tell the pilgrims plainly who you were

effects.log: The pilgrims fall silent. One, an old priestess, gives a slow nod.

choices.text: Record all of it, including what you did

effects.log: The scribe weeps on the third page and keeps writing.

events.text: The training-yard of {llg_who} was yours. You remember what was done on it. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, and {llg_cause} at the end. Moss lies thick around its border by long agreement. You cross it, and the old turf takes your footsteps as if it kept a ledger.

choices.text: Look for the families who still keep the dates

effects.log: There are a few. They let you take a spade beside them.

choices.text: Dig it over and plant it

effects.log: It takes a season. The first beans come up crooked and alive.

choices.text: Tell them who you were

effects.log: They hear it through. Nobody raises a hand against you, which is harder than a blow.

choices.text: Have the whole account written, the worst included

effects.log: The sheet fills slowly. At the foot of it, you put your name.

events.text: The grim tale of {llg_who} is yours. The tellers soften its worst chapter, and you remember that chapter exactly. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death by {llg_cause}. Every telling paints a monster, and you cannot honestly say the painting is false.

choices.text: Seek out the descendants and speak with them

effects.log: A few remain, and know the tale well. They listen to you, warily.

choices.text: Gather and burn every copy of the tale you can find

effects.log: You never find them all. The attempt itself is a kind of confession.

choices.text: Tell them to their faces who you were

effects.log: The teller stops mid-line and lowers the gourd. A long silence follows.

choices.text: Have the true account set down, uncut

effects.log: It is written. It is long. It is true.

events.text: The dark custom began with your word. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death by {llg_cause}. They turn their faces at the bend in the stair, and do not know why they do it. You do.

choices.text: Find the people it harmed and listen to them

effects.log: They are scattered, but a few come. You hear all of them out, and take no notes.

choices.text: End the custom, aloud, in front of them

effects.log: You say it plainly where they all gather. It fades slowly, then very suddenly.

choices.text: Tell them who began it

effects.log: They stare. The custom falters in front of you.

choices.text: Have the whole history written down

effects.log: The first page is the hardest. After that it goes quicker.

events.text: You tend {llg_thing} as it should be tended. Nobody asks who you are. The lamps are trimmed, the steps swept, the incense kept dry. Slowly the faithful notice that someone has been careful with the place. An old nun leaves a gift of tea at the door every dawn, and does not wait to be thanked.

choices.text: Keep it up, year on year

effects.log: The tea comes every dawn. The temple glows quietly.

choices.text: Teach a young keeper the work

effects.log: The keeper learns fast. You step back, content.

events.text: You tend the height: clear the cairns, mend the guide-rope, keep the beacon lit on stormy nights. Pilgrims begin to leave a tithe of cloth at the top. They do not know why. They do know the place feels kept.

choices.text: Keep the beacon fed

effects.log: It burns through the long winter. The pilgrims speak of a good spirit on the height.

choices.text: Plant something hardy at the top

effects.log: A twisted pine takes root. The wind has opinions.

events.text: You tend what was left, in the way that needs no name: the school's old court, the telling at the steps, the way of doing a thing. You do it without credit. Everyone assumes it was always like this, which is the highest praise you could have asked.

choices.text: Keep doing it without a word

effects.log: No one thanks you. The thing goes on.

choices.text: Let one person in on it

effects.log: A young person learns what you do and why. It will outlast you.

events.text: You tend the dark thing as one tends a grave: carefully, daily, without ceremony. The court watches, uncertain whether this is penance or presumption. After a season someone leaves a lamp at the gate. After a year, two lamps.

choices.text: Keep going, however slowly it is forgiven

effects.log: It is not forgiven. It is accepted, which is something else.

choices.text: Ask a survivor what they need

effects.log: The answer is small and simple. You provide it.

events.text: You told them. There are still beings here whose grandparents knew someone who knew {llg_who}, and they have a test ready, since you are not the first: three questions. What did {llg_he} drink at dawn? Whom did {llg_he} never forgive? What carried {llg_he} off? A hush settles over the court. No claimant has ever got all three.

choices.text: Answer as only you could

ok.log: You answer all three. The eldest sits back slowly. The court murmurs, and one by one they bow.

fail.log: You stumble on the second. They smile politely, and heads shake.

choices.text: Offer them a sample of the old skill

ok.log: The challenger yields. The stance is exactly the one in the old carving.

fail.log: The challenger is quicker than the carving implied. You go down, and the doubters nod.

choices.text: Laugh, and say it was a jest

effects.log: You laugh and call it nonsense. Some are relieved. A few are not.

events.text: You told them. By now it is only a myth in {llg_region}, and a stranger saying "I was" is a jest the courts have heard before. A solemn old priest of the myth asks about {llg_who}, and they have a test ready, since you are not the first: three questions. What did {llg_he} drink at dawn? Whom did {llg_he} never forgive? What carried {llg_he} off? A hush settles over the court. No claimant has ever got all three.
