effects.log: You laugh and call it nonsense. Some are relieved. A few are not.

events.text: You told them who you were. No one forgave anything. They listened as if you were a verdict. Some rose to leave, then did not. The silence afterward was the longest of your existence.

choices.text: Stand there and take whatever comes

effects.log: What comes is quiet and harsh. You stand through it.

choices.text: Offer to go, and stay if they say stay

effects.log: They do not say go. They do not say stay. You stay.

events.text: Scribe Anseo of the Book of Fates has ink on the cuffs and no time to spare. For nineteen ages Anseo has worked on the faults in the entry for {llg_who}. "Three of my predecessors lost their wits," the Scribe says, writing. Then Anseo reads your list, and stops. "How do you know the colour of the shutters?" You had written nothing about shutters.

choices.text: Tell the Scribe it was handed down to you

effects.log: Anseo narrows both eyes, and finally accepts it as a source, with visible reluctance.

choices.text: Tell the Scribe the truth and see what happens

effects.log: The quill goes down. "I suspected something of the kind," Anseo says. The entry is amended before the lamps are lit.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} has grown wrong in a hundred ways, and a few right ones. You go from pilgrim to pilgrim correcting small things, patiently: the date, the ending, the soup. One resists, then relents. "It is a worse tale," the pilgrim says, "and truer. I will sing the true one at the steps."

choices.text: Give the pilgrim the true verses, one by one

effects.log: The pilgrim writes them down. The steps notice the change by autumn.

choices.text: Leave the pilgrim to decide

effects.log: The pilgrim sings the false one, with a pause where the true one used to be.

events.text: You have the whole of it written down, the worst included. The Book of Fates reads it twice, and asks if you want it entered under your own name. You do not. It is entered under a number, and any scholar may find it who looks.

choices.text: Sign it, in the end, with your old name

effects.log: The old name still suits the pen. You wonder at that.

choices.text: Leave it unsigned

effects.log: It is read. It is cited. Nobody knows whose it is.

events.text: The work goes on all year: the drain they ought to have dug, the broken step, the roof. The chief mason asks whose offerings these are. Nobody's, you say. He looks at your plans, then at the old wall, then at you. "Same hand," he mutters, and decides it is none of his business. The temple holds a dinner for the unnamed donor. You are seated at the end of the table.

choices.text: Go to the dinner and eat heartily

effects.log: You eat well. They toast the donor, and you raise your teacup to the toast. It is oddly comfortable.

choices.text: Scratch a small mark on a beam where only you would look

effects.log: One tiny glyph, high under a rafter. A hundred ages on, you will find it again.

events.text: A beacon-tower goes up on the height that year, paid by an anonymous patron, built by a crew who ask no questions. On the first clear night the tower lights, and the pilgrims of {llg_region} turn to look. The old keeper says it is the best fire he has seen. You say nothing.

choices.text: Watch it light, and watch the pilgrims

effects.log: Their faces are the gift. You take it home.

choices.text: Hang a small lamp of your own beside it

effects.log: A tiny flame next to the great one. It outlasts the winter.

events.text: A roofed hall goes up beside the old drill-court: a place to rest between forms, and to practise out of the rain. The war-gods who use it give the donor a nickname, "the Dry One." You smile, and let them.

choices.text: Sit in it on a rainy day, among strangers

effects.log: The rain on the roof is the best sound. Nobody guesses.

choices.text: Add a small stove, quietly

effects.log: The stove warms the winter forms. A mystery grows round it.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} is set down on a tablet, cut by a family of carvers, and hung in the harbour hall of {llg_region}. It is not the whole tale. But the tablet will outlast the singers, and the true line is on it: the one nobody believes and everybody keeps.

choices.text: Stand in the hall and let the pilgrims come

effects.log: They come. Some read, some sing. You are the quietest listener.

choices.text: Pay the carvers an extra, secretly

effects.log: The carvers add a border of herons. Nobody asks who asked for it.

events.text: A schoolhouse for the custom goes up in {llg_region}, teaching the way to anyone who asks. It opens with nine pupils and no explanation. By spring it has forty, and a waiting list. The founder's name is not on it, which suits you perfectly.

choices.text: Watch the first lesson from the back

effects.log: The teacher stumbles once, recovers. You nod, silently.

choices.text: Leave your best scroll on the shelf

effects.log: It is found within the month, and used.

events.text: It took a season to raise and takes nine to pull down. No one helps at first. Then one morning a boy from the court with the barred doors climbs up and lifts a stone, asking nothing. His father follows. They never speak to you. When the last of the wall is gone, the whole court comes to stand in the open air where it used to be.

choices.text: Stand with them and look at the empty place

effects.log: You stand. Nobody speaks. It is the quietest and most useful hour of your existence.

choices.text: Slip away before they arrive

effects.log: You are gone by dawn. The court will wonder, for a long time, who did it.

events.text: You begin by taking the name off the map. It is easier than you expected: a few mapmakers were already uneasy. The pilgrims of {llg_region} watch the new line go in, and begin to cross the old height again. The weather is merely weather.

choices.text: Cross it yourself, once, slowly

effects.log: It is only sky. The sky does not forgive, but it does not hold on.

choices.text: Leave a quiet marker at the edge

effects.log: A small stone with a number on it. Pilgrims leave it alone.

events.text: Bit by bit you take apart what can be taken apart: the custom, the story, the sealed shrine. It is slow, plain labour and wins you no friends. Then one day a young god asks about the old business and nobody can answer, and a long-held breath leaves the heavens.

choices.text: Tell the child the plain truth, kindly

effects.log: The child listens, nods, and goes to play. That is all anyone wanted.

choices.text: Let the question lapse

effects.log: It lapses. It will not be missed.

events.text: A priestess named Sobin comes up the temple steps one autumn with a pack and a walking-staff. She tends old shrines, she says, from court to court, because someone ought to and nobody pays. She looks over your work on {llg_thing}, clicks her tongue, and hands you the end of a rope. You hold it. An hour on, you are halfway up the scaffold yourself.

choices.text: Ask what she counts as an old shrine

effects.log: She names about forty. Most lie under cloud, now. You are on her list.

choices.text: Keep holding the rope

effects.log: She works, you steady. Small talk drifts up and down the scaffold.

events.text: Priestess Sobin visits again with her apprentice Yul. She goes over your work without a word, draws a thumb across a joint, and withholds criticism, which from Sobin counts as eloquence. Yul murmurs that nobody has ever watched Sobin take a meal.

choices.text: Offer them both a hot meal

effects.log: Sobin eats a small bowl, to the astonishment of Yul. You are, quietly, adopted.

choices.text: Ask Yul how she came to this

effects.log: A short story. A long respect. You will hear the rest later.

events.text: Sobin finds a forgotten wayside shrine with its roof fallen in. She does not storm. She sits an hour studying the wreckage, then starts sorting the timbers by length. Yul, grimly merry, passes you a mallet. "It always starts like this," Yul says.

choices.text: Take the mallet and begin

effects.log: It is two weeks of work and an unreasonable amount of tea. The roof goes up.

choices.text: Sit with Sobin and say nothing

effects.log: You sit. Something about the silence is helpful.

events.text: A rich young god arrives to inspect {llg_thing} with a retinue, a poet and a plan to have it gilded. His permits are in order. Sobin plants herself before him with her staff and is walked around. He asks you, whom he takes for the foreman, where the gilders should start. A pendant at his throat bears the name of {llg_who}.

choices.text: Point him to the real rot and let his offerings go there

effects.log: He is more embarrassed than offended. The offerings go to the right beams, and the pendant stays on.

choices.text: Gently talk him out of the gilding

ok.log: You walk him through the whole place. By the end he is carrying a bucket. Sobin pats your arm in passing.

fail.log: He will not be moved. The gilders start on the wrong wall, and Sobin sighs for a season.

events.text: Age has caught Sobin. Seated on the step of {llg_thing}, she watches Yul work and lists, unasked, who is to have her tools when she is gone. You write it down. "You will do this better than I did," she says. It is no compliment; it is a bequest.

choices.text: Promise to keep the tools in use

effects.log: The promise is easy. Keeping it will take the rest of your existence.

choices.text: Say she has ages left yet

effects.log: She snorts. She does not have, and you both know it.

events.text: A broad godling with a ferryman's hands arrives at your door: Cheon Ma-ra. His shrine has kept an account for five ages, and he wants to read it out to whoever now looks after {llg_thing}, being the nearest thing to the responsible party. He sits and reads for three hours. Names and years, and nothing else. He never lifts his voice.

choices.text: Listen to the end and ask him for a copy

effects.log: He hands it over. The paper is soft as cloth with handling. You keep it.

choices.text: Remark that all this was a very long time ago

effects.log: He regards you for a long moment. "Yes," he says. "That is what we all say, in the end." He leaves.

events.text: Cheon Ma-ra has pieced it together, or enough of it. Nobody ever learns how. He climbs the steps at dusk with a boat-hook in one hand, unhurried, and says he is not a fool and does not know how such things can be, but his grandmother told him what to look for. He says your hands are the same hands. He has come far. He lays the hook down between you.

choices.text: Kneel and leave the hook where it lies

effects.log: He looks at you a long while. Then he takes the hook and goes down the steps. It is not forgiveness. It is a beginning.

choices.text: Tell him what you have made of this life, and let him judge

ok.log: He hears all of it. He weighs it. He nods once and takes up the hook.

fail.log: He weighs it, and finds it light, and leaves the hook behind, which is a small mercy.

events.text: Cheon Ma-ra sends word that his daughter will carry the reckoning from now on. He is tired, he says, and the book is heavy. A small godling with serious eyes appears at the gate with a satchel, and asks if she may read you the first name. She reads it clearly. She has been practising.

choices.text: Listen to all the names, however long it takes

effects.log: It takes an afternoon. She does not hurry, and neither do you.

choices.text: Ask her to read slowly, so you can remember them

effects.log: She slows. By dusk you can say a dozen of them yourself.

events.text: The reckoning has been carried to the last of the line, an old goddess who writes poorly and reads with a finger. She brings you a gift: a spare copy, so that two shrines hold it. You understand the gesture. It is a trust, or a sentence, or both. You take it in both hands.

choices.text: Promise to keep it where the next generation can find it

effects.log: You promise, and keep it, and the next generation does find it.

choices.text: Offer to add your own page at the end

effects.log: She nods, and gives you a pen. You write for an hour.

events.text: You have grown old tending {llg_thing}. The court has adopted you as a fixture; young godlings wave. At the evening offering an old pilgrim asks if the place is quiet. "It is," you say, and look at the stair, and for a moment know every foot that ever climbed it. The tea is hot. The air is clean.

choices.text: Sit a while longer

effects.log: The light turns gold. Somebody is sweeping, far off.

choices.text: Say good evening to the stair

effects.log: The stair does not answer. You do not mind.

events.text: Late in existence you are still being asked to prove it, now and again, by cheerful young scholars with tablets. You do. Sometimes they believe you. Sometimes they say "how marvellous" and write down something else. It no longer troubles you. The place knows. That is enough.

choices.text: Answer one more question, graciously

effects.log: You answer. The scholar writes it down, half-believing.

choices.text: Close the door gently on the tablet

effects.log: You close it. The lamp on the table is warm.

events.text: Your corrections have become the standard entry. The Book of Fates now carries them, and young gods learn the true dates. You pass through the record hall once a year on pilgrimage. Nobody there knows you; the clerk bows at the door, and that is all it takes.

choices.text: Leave a small note on the desk of the clerk

effects.log: The note says only thanks. The clerk will puzzle over it for a season.

choices.text: Walk out into the evening

effects.log: The evening is mild. The Book is right, and that is quietly enough.

events.text: The hall you built still stands, a little weathered. Young godlings play on its steps, ignorant of whoever paid for it. The roof does not leak. You watch from across the court with a cup of nectar, and the roof is the best thing you ever did.

choices.text: Pay for the next repair, quietly

effects.log: It is done by someone who does not ask. The roof holds.

choices.text: Watch the young ones

effects.log: They run in and out of the rain. You smile like a fool.

events.text: You tried to atone, and the ages have worn on, and the work is not finished, and never will be. A younger deity has taken up the broom. You tell them what you know. They write it down, and do not ask for more, and that is all you can ask.

choices.text: Hand over the broom

effects.log: It is lighter than you remembered. The younger one holds it with care.

choices.text: Keep sweeping, since you can still

effects.log: You sweep a little each morning. The stair is cleaner for it.

events.text: It is gone, the thing you tore down. Where it stood is a garden now, and a cloud of bees, and a little tablet nobody reads. You visit on warm days. The air is clear. You do not forgive yourself, but you have stopped waiting for the day you would.

choices.text: Sit among the bees

effects.log: They tolerate you. You doze a little.

choices.text: Pull a weed or two

effects.log: A small job, and good. The garden is yours to weed, if not to own.

events.text: You have not visited in ages. It still stands, you hear: {llg_thing}, in {llg_region}. Only last week at the exchange a stranger told it wrongly, and you let it pass. Then you paid for the whole table without explaining, and walked out into the chill feeling lighter than you had any right to feel.

choices.text: Walk home the long way round

effects.log: The long way is longer than you remember. It is worth every step.

choices.text: Go back inside and hear how it ends

effects.log: The ending is worse than you feared, and better told.

events.text: A tellman called Boram works the harvest market with a pair of spoons for a clapper. Today it is {llg_who}, who lived to {llg_told_age} and left {llg_thing} in {llg_region}, "not {llg_years} years gone, and my own aunt whitewashed its walls." Boram tells it nearly straight. You stay after the buyers drift off, and could not say why.

choices.text: Stay to the end and ask where it stands

effects.log: Boram names the road and charges you a copper for it. You remember the road regardless.

choices.text: Toss a copper and move on

effects.log: Boram bites it, nods, and clacks the spoons. The name stays with you like a burr in a sock.

events.text: "And when {llg_who} came to {llg_region}, the hills knelt down," cries Boram, spoons in the air. "So they built {llg_thing} on the spot where the hills knelt. {llg_He} lived {llg_told_age} years and never once slept lying down." You think nobody could be so daft, and feel annoyed, and cannot think why.

choices.text: Say that nobody could live that way

effects.log: "You have seen it, have you?" says Boram, and the market laughs. For a moment you had the oddest feeling you had.

choices.text: Ask what the folk do at the hall these days

effects.log: They light tapers and ask for sons, and for rain, says Boram. Mostly neither comes. They go on asking.

events.text: On the drovers' map a hill in {llg_region} has a new name. They call it {llg_thing}, after {llg_who}, and an old drover who remembers being told says {llg_he} died of {llg_cause}. He spits for luck. The name passes through you for no reason at all, and you ask him to say it again.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} was like

effects.log: "Short-tempered," says the drover. "Or tall. One of those." You laugh, and cannot think why you are so pleased.

choices.text: Copy the name onto your wrist

effects.log: It washes off in a week. By then you have looked at it plenty.

events.text: There is an old skipping rhyme for counting the hills of {llg_region}, and every child knows it. {llg_Thing} is the third. Only when nearly grown do you think to ask what the word means, and a grandmother says it is a word for a kind of giant, from before the first plough. It does not sound like a giant to you.

choices.text: Say the rhyme over until the word stops meaning anything

effects.log: It does not stop. You leave it for now. It has waited this long.

choices.text: Go back to the skipping game

effects.log: You miss the rope on the third hill. You always will now. The others find it very funny.

events.text: An old soldier at the ale-house has a limp and a story. He trained, he says, at {llg_thing} in {llg_region} under a master who trained under {llg_who}, {llg_years} years gone. "Stones worn to the shape of a stance. Stand in the hollows and your feet will learn." You notice you are already standing the way he means.

choices.text: Ask him to show the footwork

effects.log: He shows you badly, and corrects himself. You correct him too, and neither of you knows how you knew.

choices.text: Stand him one more mug and listen

effects.log: He tells it three more ways. In all of them the stones are the same.

events.text: They say all fighting began at {llg_thing}, in {llg_region}, when the first of the old gods picked a quarrel with a boulder, and every school in the world claims descent. {llg_who} is the name they give that god. In the kingdom's schools they have written six volumes on what the name means. In the village they bake it into loaves.

choices.text: Buy a loaf

effects.log: A good loaf. The stamp is a little figure in a stance. You study the feet a long time, and they are wrong.

choices.text: Ask who taught the god

effects.log: The baker laughs until she must sit down. You meant it as a real question.

events.text: A ballad is making the rounds, "{llg_song}." "{llg_verse}," Boram sings. It is about {llg_who}, who died at {llg_told_age} of {llg_cause}, the tellman swears. You have never heard it. You know how the next verse goes before it is sung, and when Boram gets it wrong, you wince.

choices.text: Sing the next verse along

effects.log: You get it right, and Boram stops and stares. "Who taught you that?" You have no answer. A dumpling is offered, warily.

choices.text: Keep quiet and pay the tellman

effects.log: A fine song. You hum it a week and it does you no harm.

events.text: These days the Tale of {llg_who} takes three nights at the fair. The first night {llg_he} wrestles a flood. The second {llg_he} weds, depending on the valley, a princess or a fox. The third {llg_he} dies of {llg_cause} at {llg_told_age} and the whole tent weeps. You weep too. It seems a very silly story.

choices.text: Go back all three nights

effects.log: It costs you most of a week. The fox is the best part. You remember no fox, and it is odd not to.

choices.text: Ask Boram how much is true

effects.log: "All of it," says Boram, "by now." That seems an answer. In time you decide it is.

events.text: People in {llg_region} perform it in one particular way, and have for {llg_years} years by their own count: a flick of the wrist, three breaths first, the old tally. Ask who began it and you get a shrug. You look on, and your hands are already doing it behind your back.

choices.text: Ask them to show you

effects.log: They show you, and you do it better than they. They assume you had a teacher from there. You let them.

choices.text: Stop your hands and walk on

effects.log: Your hands stop. They go on thinking about it all that week.

events.text: Everyone does it, in {llg_region}. It is simply how it is done, like salt in the soup. Scholars have proved it comes from the very first morning. Nobody knows it comes from anybody, and if you told them they would be polite and carry on. You catch yourself doing it wrong, then correct it, and you have never been there.

choices.text: Try it their way, on purpose

effects.log: It is, unfortunately, a very good way. You do not know why that makes you so happy.

choices.text: Think about something else

effects.log: You do. Your hands, you notice, do not.

events.text: They do not say the name of {llg_who} in {llg_region} after dark. Boram will, for double, in a low voice: how {llg_he} held the district in a fist, and how {llg_thing} is shut, and how no one has dared pull it down in {llg_years} years in case it notices. Your stomach goes cold. You pay the double.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} did

effects.log: Boram tells you a little. It is enough. You do not sleep well, and wish you knew why it sounds like your own name.

choices.text: Say it was a long time ago

effects.log: It was. Nobody thanks you for saying so, and you leave faster than you meant to.

events.text: There is a cold pass in {llg_region} that the maps call {llg_thing}. Carters go a day around it. They say {llg_who} did something there, {llg_years} years back or more, to the folk who lived beneath. None will say what. All of them look at the ground as they don't say it, and you do too.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} did

effects.log: They tell you a little. It is enough. You do not sleep well, and wonder why it feels like your own name.

choices.text: Say it was a long time ago

effects.log: It was. Nobody thanks you for saying so.

events.text: The soldiers' tale of {llg_who} has teeth and no thunder now: where {llg_he} trained, what {llg_he} did to those {llg_he} trained, and how the ground at {llg_thing} is still kept clear because no one wants to stand on it.

choices.text: Ask who was hurt by it

effects.log: A long list, they say. They give you three names, and the three stay with you.

choices.text: Keep walking

effects.log: You keep walking. It does not make the road any shorter.

events.text: Every child in {llg_region} knows what {llg_who} will do if they do not come in at dusk. Boram's telling has more teeth than that. {llg_He} lived to {llg_told_age} on other people's years, and there is a village with no one in it. You listen with a sick feeling and find you are checking the tale for mistakes.

choices.text: Ask what {llg_he} did

effects.log: They tell you a little. It is enough. You do not sleep well.

choices.text: Say it was a long time ago

effects.log: It was. Nobody thanks you for saying so.

events.text: They keep doing it in {llg_region}, and at last you learn its purpose. A long-memoried neighbour explains that {llg_thing} started as proof you had settled your debt to {llg_who}. The gesture survived. The dread behind it has not.

choices.text: Ask who was hurt by it

effects.log: A long list, they say. They give you three names, and the three stay with you.

choices.text: Keep walking

effects.log: You keep walking. It does not make the road any shorter.

events.text: The parish roll entry on {llg_who} is read aloud in the schoolhouse of {llg_region} every year. It gives the dates, the age ({llg_age}) and the cause, {llg_cause}. It is the dullest thing you have ever heard. Boram's spoons can be heard through the wall, doing the dragon. Someone, you feel, went to great trouble to make this boring.

choices.text: Stay and hear the dates through

effects.log: You are the only one who stays. The teacher gives you a look of pure gratitude.

choices.text: Go and listen to the spoons

effects.log: The spoons are a good deal more fun and a good deal less accurate. You come away knowing both.

events.text: A pilgrim cart comes through with a broken axle, on its way to {llg_region} to see {llg_thing}. You help them lift it. An old woman on the tailboard looks you over and pats the plank beside her. "You have the look," she says. "Come along. It is only a few weeks."

choices.text: Climb up

effects.log: The cart lurches off. You are on the way before you have decided to go.

choices.text: Wave them off

effects.log: They roll out of sight. You feel the pull for days.

events.text: A shopkeeper needs someone to carry a sealed letter to {llg_region}, good pay, no questions. Only after most of a day's thinking do you notice that you meant to go there anyway, and have meant to since you first heard of {llg_thing}.

choices.text: Take the letter

effects.log: The seal is warm in your hand. You leave on the evening coach.

choices.text: Let someone else carry it

effects.log: Someone does. You regret it, mildly, for weeks.

events.text: You keep dreaming of a hillside you have never seen. It is not a remarkable dream: you are climbing steps, your knee hurts, you have something to do when you reach the top. You wake cross every time. This has gone on a year, and {llg_region} is the only place you can think of it belonging.

choices.text: Go to {llg_region} and get it over with

effects.log: You set out the next morning. The dream does not come that night.

choices.text: Drink something warm before bed and stay put

effects.log: It helps a little. It does not help enough.

events.text: The school you once founded in a past life still drills at {llg_Thing} in {llg_region}: a yard of worn flagstones, with the pupils in rows. Nobody knows the founder's face. Your feet know where the fourth flag dips. The master nods to you across the yard and does not ask your name.

choices.text: Stand in the hollows and let your feet remember

effects.log: They remember a good deal more than you do. You leave the yard slowly.

choices.text: Ask the gatekeeper whose school this was

effects.log: The gatekeeper gives a name you almost say along with him.

events.text: The old way of {llg_region} was handed down, through you, to people who still do it. A farmer at the roadside shows you the first form of it, shyly, and your hands go along with him before you can decide. He looks up, startled, and then at his own hands. "Odd," he says. "You do it like my grandfather."

choices.text: Do the second form, since your hands insist

effects.log: The farmer follows. You finish together, in the dust, and he does not ask.

choices.text: Say it is a common way of doing it

effects.log: He nods. He does not believe you. It is a very pleasant lie.

events.text: The hall of the school you once headed stands in {llg_region}, and the pupils burn a taper to a founder-head whose name has worn off the board. The taper-smoke goes straight up. You know the hall's smell: wax, damp, hay. The caretaker watches you stand a moment too long at the lintel.

choices.text: Light a taper and stand where the pupils stand

effects.log: The smoke rises straight. The caretaker breathes out.

choices.text: Ask the caretaker how long the hall has stood

effects.log: A number of years, and a story. The story is nearly right.

events.text: A hill in {llg_region} carries your old family's name, and the family that keeps its orchard will tell you, over cider, that the founder's ghost counts the apples. The cider is the right kind. You know the orchard path without being shown, and the keeper watches you know it.

choices.text: Admit you feel as though you have been here

effects.log: The keeper smiles as at a familiar embarrassment. "Everyone does, the first time," comes the answer.

choices.text: Say nothing and finish the cider

effects.log: You finish it. It tastes of your own long-ago kitchen.

events.text: A great hill in {llg_region} is called the King's Seat, though no king sits there now, and the road up is wider than the traffic needs. The locals say a ruler once came this way and ordered it so. You walk the road with your hands in your sleeves, as someone does who is used to being carried.

choices.text: Climb to the top and look at the view

effects.log: It is the view of someone who ruled it. You come down quieter.

choices.text: Ask the toll-keeper who the ruler was

effects.log: He gives a name and a cough. The name is nearly yours.

events.text: You come to {llg_region} and find that your fame has outlived your face. A ballad, a puppet play and a name on a pie-seller's cart: "{llg_who}'s Fair Pies." The pie is good. The legend is vaguely, endearingly wrong, and you eat it sitting on the kerb.

choices.text: Tell the pie-seller the real story

effects.log: She listens, nods, and says it is a better story than hers. She keeps selling hers.

choices.text: Eat your pie and keep quiet

effects.log: It is a very good pie. Its legend does you no harm.

events.text: A shuttered hall stands in {llg_region}: {llg_thing}. Nobody will tell you why it is shut, but everyone knows. Your feet know the steps anyway, and your hand knows the bolt. You stand at the door with a coldness in the chest, as if you were the one who had to close it.

choices.text: Ask who still remembers it

effects.log: A few, it turns out. They do not like being asked, and they answer.

choices.text: Walk away from the door

effects.log: You walk. The door seems to watch you go.

events.text: The hill the carters call {llg_thing} is empty of anything but weather. Nobody lingers there. You climb to the top and feel the old guilt of a place once used for something, and now only high.

choices.text: Stay a while and see what rises in you

effects.log: It rises, slowly, and it is not pleasant. You write down some of it.

choices.text: Leave a cairn and go

effects.log: Three stones, stacked. You do not know what for.

events.text: {llg_Thing} is kept clear by common consent. Grass grows round it, not on it. Soldiers who pass bow stiffly and walk the long way. Your own steps take you across it before you notice, and the grass, you see, has made you a path.

choices.text: Stop in the middle and stand quiet

effects.log: The air is cold and attentive. Something decides you may leave.

choices.text: Cross it faster

effects.log: You cross. The back of your neck does not forgive you.

events.text: The Tale of {llg_who} is told in {llg_region} with the spoons muffled, in a voice for secrets. It is not a long tale. Every listener leaves quieter than they came, and you know every pause in it before the teller reaches it.

choices.text: Ask the teller where the tale came from

effects.log: From those who lived it, comes the answer. That is all anyone says.

choices.text: Leave a coin and go

effects.log: The coin is taken without a word.

events.text: A custom in {llg_region} has everyone avert their eyes at a certain bend of the lane, and nobody can say why. You find your own eyes lowering before you reach it. Underneath your sleeve your wrist remembers something it should not.

choices.text: Keep your eyes up, and see what is there

effects.log: A blank wall, and a sense of being watched by it. You make yourself stay.

choices.text: Lower your eyes with the rest

effects.log: You do. It is easy, and that is what troubles you.

events.text: You have stood on this step before; not in this body. {llg_Thing} is smaller than you remember, or you are larger, and the incense is a different kind. A young caretaker looks at you, then at the lintel, then at you, with the face of someone who has just remembered a name.

choices.text: Ask the caretaker what they remember

effects.log: Nothing, they say, nothing, and then, slowly, a great deal.

choices.text: Light a taper and say nothing

effects.log: The smoke rises straight. Somebody nearby breathes out.

events.text: The hill is called by another name now, but your eyes find the old line of it from far off, and your ribs ache in a way that does not belong to this body. You have been here before, in another life, and the sky has kept your shape in it.

choices.text: Climb up and look at the view

effects.log: It is the same view. It has been waiting.

choices.text: Turn back; one memory at a time

effects.log: You turn, slowly. The ache stays a day, then fades.

events.text: The yard in {llg_region} has new flagstones laid over old, and under them, somewhere, your own footprints. You feel them through the soles. A pupil stops mid-form and stares, and then recovers, and bows.

choices.text: Take the stance and hold it a moment

effects.log: The stance fits like a glove worn by someone else. The pupil does not stop staring.

choices.text: Walk the edge, and leave it to them

effects.log: You leave it to them. They do not know what they are standing on.

events.text: A tellman in {llg_region} is telling a tale you ought not to know the ending of, and do. You listen to the end, with the odd sense of seeing the last page of your own book. The tellman looks at you across the lamps and falters, once.

choices.text: Wait for the tellman afterward

effects.log: The tellman says the tale has a "true" version nobody can find. You nod, and say nothing.

choices.text: Slip out before the last verse

effects.log: You leave. You can hear the verse from the street.

events.text: Everyone in {llg_region} still does it the old way, and your hands join in without asking you. A woman beside you says, "You have done this before," as one remarks on the weather, and she is quite right.

choices.text: Ask her who showed her

effects.log: The somebody of her grandmother, she says. You nod, and keep doing it.

choices.text: Keep doing it, and say nothing

effects.log: It is a comfortable silence. Your hands know more than you do.

events.text: Somebody has been adding to {llg_thing} in this body's absence, and you know the hand: a better rail where the steps are slick, a patched roof, and a tiny thing tucked out of sight that only you would think to look for. You paid in silver, in some life you can only half grasp, and you did not sign.

choices.text: Leave it exactly as it is

effects.log: You leave it. The tiny thing sits where you put it.

choices.text: Fix the one thing you got wrong

effects.log: Three screws and an afternoon. It was always that small.

events.text: This ground has felt your weight before. {llg_Thing} looks smaller, or you have grown, and the folk who study their boots are not the same folk, yet the heaviness stays. A chill goes through you. Here is where you did what you did, and each stone has kept the record.

choices.text: Stay and let it be heavy

effects.log: It is. You stay longer than you can bear, and a little longer.

choices.text: Leave quietly, and come back with a plan

effects.log: You leave. You will come back, you promise, and it feels like a vow.

events.text: It strikes on a drizzly night, on the chapel steps, without warning. You know how that wall was laid, because you fought about it. You know the creak of the third stair. {llg_name}. That was your name: {llg_age} years under it, a death of {llg_cause}, and now tapers are lit to it inside and prayers for rain are put to it.

choices.text: Pick up a broom and say nothing

effects.log: You sweep. The act is its own answer.

choices.text: Go in and tell them who you are

effects.log: Heads turn. Some listen, some laugh, one weeps.

choices.text: Find whoever keeps the roll, and put them right

effects.log: The registrar takes notes, coldly at first, then with trembling hands.

choices.text: Pay 200 taels for what it should have had from the start

effects.log: The coin changes hands; the roof is mended by autumn.

events.text: You are standing on the ridge when it arrives. This was your hill. You named it from a cart-seat, on a morning with a cold in your head. {llg_name}: you lived {llg_age} years, died of {llg_cause}, and now the carters call it by your title and have no idea.

choices.text: Plant a marker and tend it quietly

effects.log: A small cairn, kept clean. The carters take it for a custom.

choices.text: Tell the next carter who you are

effects.log: They stare, then laugh, then do not laugh.

choices.text: Go to the survey office and correct the name

effects.log: The surveyors listen, appalled and fascinated.

choices.text: Pay 200 taels for a proper beacon on the summit

effects.log: A beacon is raised by midwinter.

events.text: The practice-yard is yours. You knew it the moment you set foot on it. {llg_name}: you taught here, bled here, were buried near here after {llg_age} years and a death of {llg_cause}. Pupils practise your stance without knowing whose it is. A boy gets it slightly wrong, and you ache to correct him.

choices.text: Take a rake and keep the yard in order

effects.log: You rake until dusk. It is the best day you have had in a while.

choices.text: Show them whose stance it is

effects.log: You do the form. Nobody breathes.

choices.text: Write the true lineage down for the school

effects.log: The senior listens and takes it in, line by line.

choices.text: Pay 200 taels to roof the practice hall

effects.log: The coin is paid. The rain stops coming through.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} is yours; it was sung about you. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}, and a ballad that got half of it wrong in lovely ways. You hear the tellman start the third night and mouth the words, and know them better than the tellman.

choices.text: Sit at the back and let it be sung

effects.log: You sit. It is strange to be moved by your own life.

choices.text: Stand up at the end and name yourself

effects.log: The tellman drops the spoons. The audience cannot decide.

choices.text: Take the tellman aside and correct the verses

effects.log: The tellman is thrilled and furious in equal measure.

choices.text: Pay 200 taels to have the tale printed

effects.log: It is printed by the next spring.

events.text: The long-kept custom of {llg_region} started with you. Your own hands did it first, on a freezing morning, only to warm themselves. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}, and a small motion that has outlived everything grander you managed.

choices.text: Keep doing it, quietly, in the right way

effects.log: You do it right, and say nothing. The old people nod.

choices.text: Tell them it was yours

effects.log: Someone says "of course it was." It is not the answer you expected.

choices.text: Teach the teachers the first form

effects.log: The first form is nearly lost. You give it back.

choices.text: Pay 200 taels for a hall to teach it in

effects.log: The hall is built and the doors stay open.

events.text: You are looking at the hall door when it arrives. You know what is behind it. You know because you had it built, and you were {llg_name}, and you remember the sound it made shutting on people. You lived {llg_age} years. There are villages here that bolt their shutters to this day, and they are right.

choices.text: Find who is left, and do what can be done

effects.log: A few. They do not forgive. They let you help.

choices.text: Pull it down: this much is in your hands

effects.log: You begin with the roof beams. The village watches, silent.

choices.text: Tell them to their faces who you were

effects.log: Some leave. Some stay to hear all of it.

choices.text: Get the whole of it written down, the worst included

effects.log: It takes a season. It is read aloud once.

events.text: The cold pass is yours. You know what you did there. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years and a death of {llg_cause}, and a thing that the carters will not cross. You stand on the edge of it, feeling the weight of that sky.

choices.text: Find who is left, and do what can be done

effects.log: There are descendants in a far village. They accept the help in silence.

choices.text: Raze the last of what remains

effects.log: It takes a season. The emptiness is cleaner.

choices.text: Tell them to their faces who you were

effects.log: The carters stop. One, an old woman, nods.

choices.text: Get the whole of it written down, the worst included

effects.log: The clerk weeps by the third page and continues.

events.text: The yard of {llg_who} is yours, and you remember what happened on it. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years and a death of {llg_cause}. The grass grows round it by agreement. You cross it, and it knows your feet.

choices.text: Find who is left, and do what can be done

effects.log: There are families who still keep the dates. They accept your hands on the work.

choices.text: Dig it up and turn it to garden

effects.log: It takes a season. The first beans come up crooked and alive.

choices.text: Tell them to their faces who you were

effects.log: They hear you out. No one lays a hand on you, which is worse.

choices.text: Get the whole of it written down, the worst included

effects.log: The page fills slowly. You sign it.

events.text: The black story of {llg_who} is yours, and the teller trims its worst part, and you recall that part to the letter. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}. Every telling paints a brute, and you cannot say the portrait is unfair.

choices.text: Find who is left, and do what can be done

effects.log: A few descendants, and they know the tale well. They listen to you, warily.

choices.text: Burn every copy of the tale you can find

effects.log: You do not find them all. The attempt is its own confession.

choices.text: Tell them to their faces who you were

effects.log: The teller stops, lowers the spoons. A silence follows.

choices.text: Get the whole of it written down, the worst included

effects.log: It is written. It is long. It is true.

events.text: The dark custom is yours; it began with your orders. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}. They avert their eyes at the bend of the lane because of you, and do not know it.

choices.text: Find who is left, and do what can be done

effects.log: They are scattered, but some come. You listen to all of them.

choices.text: End the custom: say so, aloud

effects.log: You say it where they can hear. It goes slowly, then at once.

choices.text: Tell them to their faces who you were

effects.log: They stare. The custom falters.

choices.text: Get the whole of it written down, the worst included

effects.log: The first page is the hardest.

events.text: You tend {llg_thing} as it should be tended. Nobody asks who you are. The tapers are trimmed, the steps swept, the straw kept dry. Slowly the pilgrims notice that someone has been careful with the place. An old widow leaves a loaf at the door every dawn, and does not wait to be thanked.

choices.text: Keep it up, year on year

effects.log: The loaf comes every dawn. The hall glows quietly.

choices.text: Teach a young keeper the work

effects.log: The keeper learns fast. You step back, content.

events.text: You tend the hill: clear the cairns, mend the guide-rope, keep the beacon lit on stormy nights. Carters begin to leave a tithe of grain at the top. They do not know why. They do know the place feels kept.

choices.text: Keep the beacon fed

effects.log: It burns through the long winter. The carters speak of a good spirit on the hill.

choices.text: Plant something hardy at the top

effects.log: A twisted pine takes root. The wind has opinions.

events.text: You tend what was left, in the way that needs no name: the school's old yard, the telling at the market, the way of doing a thing. You do it without credit. Everyone assumes it was always like this, which is the highest praise you could have asked.

choices.text: Keep doing it without a word

effects.log: No one thanks you. The thing goes on.

choices.text: Let one person in on it

effects.log: A young person learns what you do and why. It will outlast you.

events.text: You tend the dark thing as one tends a grave: carefully, daily, without ceremony. The village watches, uncertain whether this is penance or presumption. After a season someone leaves a lantern at the gate. After a year, two lanterns.

choices.text: Keep going, however slowly it is forgiven

effects.log: It is not forgiven. It is accepted, which is something else.

choices.text: Ask a survivor what they need

effects.log: The answer is small and simple. You provide it.

events.text: You told them. There are still people here whose grandparents knew someone who knew {llg_who}, and they have a test ready, since you are not the first: three questions. What did {llg_he} drink at dawn? Whom did {llg_he} never forgive? What carried {llg_he} off? A hush falls over the yard.

choices.text: Answer as only you could

ok.log: You answer all three. The eldest sits back slowly. The court murmurs, and one by one they bow.

fail.log: You stumble on the second. They smile politely, and heads shake.

choices.text: Offer them a sample of the old skill

ok.log: The challenger yields. The stance is exactly the one in the old carving.

fail.log: The challenger is quicker than the carving implied. You go down, and the doubters nod.

effects.log: You laugh and call it nonsense. Some are relieved. A few are not.

events.text: You told them. By now it is only a myth in {llg_region}, and a stranger saying "I was" is a jest the valleys have heard before. A solemn old keeper of the myth asks about {llg_who}, and they have a test ready, since you are not the first: three questions. What did {llg_he} drink at dawn? Whom did {llg_he} never forgive? What carried {llg_he} off? A hush falls over the yard.

fail.log: You stumble on the second. They smile politely, and heads shake.

effects.log: You laugh and call it nonsense. Some are relieved. A few are not.

events.text: You told them who you were. No one forgave anything. They listened as if you were a verdict. Some rose to leave, then did not. The silence afterward was the longest of your lives.

choices.text: Stand there and take whatever comes

effects.log: What comes is quiet and harsh. You stand through it.

choices.text: Offer to go, and stay if they say stay

effects.log: They do not say go. They do not say stay. You stay.

events.text: Registrar Dae Hyeona of the district rolls is a thin woman with ink on her cuffs and no patience. She has spent nineteen years on the errors in the entry for {llg_who}. "Three of my predecessors went mad," she says, without looking up. Then she reads your list, and looks up. "How do you know about the soup?" You had not written down any soup.

choices.text: Tell her it was handed down to you

effects.log: She narrows her eyes, and accepts it, grudgingly, as a source.

choices.text: Tell her the truth, and see what she does

effects.log: She sets down her pen. "I thought it might be something like that," she says. The entry is amended before dusk.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} has grown wrong in a hundred ways, and a few right ones. You go from tellman to tellman correcting small things, patiently: the date, the ending, the soup. One resists, then relents. "It is a worse tale," he says, "and truer. I will tell the true one at the fair."

choices.text: Give him the true verses, one by one

effects.log: He writes them down. The fair notices the change by autumn.

choices.text: Leave him to decide

effects.log: He tells the false one, with a pause where the true one used to be.

events.text: You have the whole of it written down, the worst included. The district rolls read it twice, and the registrar asks if you want it entered under your own name. You do not. It is entered under a number, and any scholar may find it who looks.

choices.text: Sign it, in the end, with your old name

effects.log: The old name still suits the pen. You wonder at that.

choices.text: Leave it unsigned

effects.log: It is read. It is cited. Nobody knows whose it is.

events.text: The work goes on all that year: the drain they should have dug, the bad step, the roof. The master mason asks who is paying. A nobody, you tell him. He looks at the plans you gave him, and at the old wall, and at you. "Same hand," he says. Then he shrugs: he is being paid. The hall holds a supper for the anonymous donor, and you are seated at the far end.

choices.text: Go to the supper, and eat a great deal

effects.log: You eat. They toast the anonymous donor. It is oddly comfortable.

choices.text: Carve something small where only you would look

effects.log: A single mark under a rafter. You will find it again in a hundred years.

events.text: A beacon-tower goes up on the hill that year, paid by an anonymous patron, built by a crew who ask no questions. On the first clear night the tower lights, and the carters of {llg_region} turn to look. The old keeper says it is the best fire he has seen. You say nothing.

choices.text: Watch it light, and watch the carters

effects.log: Their faces are the gift. You take it home.

choices.text: Hang a small lantern of your own beside it

effects.log: A tiny flame next to the great one. It outlasts the winter.

events.text: A roofed hall goes up beside the old yard: a place to rest between forms, and to practise out of the rain. The soldiers who use it give the donor a nickname, "the Dry One." You smile, and let them.

choices.text: Sit in it on a rainy day, among strangers

effects.log: The rain on the roof is the best sound. Nobody guesses.

choices.text: Add a small stove, quietly

effects.log: The stove warms the winter forms. A mystery grows round it.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} is set down in print, bound by a family of binders, and hung in the market hall of {llg_region}. It is not the whole tale. But the sheet will outlast the tellmen, and the true line is on it: the one nobody believes and everybody keeps.

choices.text: Stand in the hall and let the tellmen come

effects.log: They come. Some read, some sing. You are the quietest listener.

choices.text: Pay the binders an extra, secretly

effects.log: The binders add a border of foxes. Nobody asks who asked for it.

events.text: A teaching house for the custom opens in {llg_region}, open to all comers. It begins with nine pupils and no speeches; by spring there are forty and a queue. The founder's name appears nowhere, which suits you down to the ground.

choices.text: Watch the first lesson from the back

effects.log: The teacher stumbles once, recovers. You nod, silently.

choices.text: Leave your best book on the shelf

effects.log: It is found within the month, and used.

events.text: It goes up in a season and comes down in nine. Nobody helps at first. Then one morning a boy from the village with the shutters has come up and picked up a stone without asking what you are about. His father comes next. They do not speak to you. On the day the last of the wall is gone, the whole village walks up to look at the empty air.

choices.text: Stand with them, and look at it

effects.log: You stand. No one speaks. It is the quietest, most useful hour of your life.

choices.text: Be gone before they come up

effects.log: You are gone. The village will wonder who did it.

events.text: You begin by taking the name off the map. It is easier than you expected: a few surveyors were already uneasy. The carters of {llg_region} watch the new line go in, and begin to cross the old pass again. The weather is merely weather.

choices.text: Cross it yourself, once, slowly

effects.log: It is only a pass. The pass does not forgive, but it does not hold on.

choices.text: Leave a quiet marker at the edge

effects.log: A small stone with a number on it. Carters leave it alone.

events.text: You undo what can be undone, piece by piece: the custom, the tale, the shuttered hall. It is slow, unglamorous work, and it makes you no friends. But a day comes when a child asks about the old thing and no one knows what to say, and you feel a long breath go out of the world.

choices.text: Tell the child the plain truth, kindly

effects.log: The child listens, nods, and goes to play. That is all anyone wanted.

choices.text: Let the question lapse

effects.log: It lapses. It will not be missed.

events.text: An old woman called Oksun arrives one autumn with a bundle and a staff. She goes from village to village seeing to the old places, she says, because someone must, and nobody pays her. She looks at what you have been doing to {llg_thing}, grunts, and asks you to hold the ladder. You hold the ladder. An hour later you are the one up it.

choices.text: Ask what she means by "old places"

effects.log: She tells you about forty of them. Most are overgrown. You are on the list now.

choices.text: Go on holding the ladder

effects.log: She works, you steady. Small talk happens up the rungs.

events.text: Granny Oksun drops in once more, her apprentice Kkachi in tow. She goes over your work wordlessly, drags a thumb across a joint, and offers no complaint, which from Oksun is practically a speech. Kkachi whispers that nobody has ever seen Oksun eat.

choices.text: Offer them both a hot meal

effects.log: Oksun eats a small bowl, to the astonishment of Kkachi. You are, quietly, adopted.

choices.text: Ask Kkachi how she came to this

effects.log: A short story. A long respect. You will hear the rest later.

events.text: Oksun arrives to find the roof of a half-forgotten shrine fallen in. She does not rage. She sits and looks at it for an hour, then begins to sort the beams. Kkachi, grimly cheerful, hands you a mallet. "This is how it always begins," she says.

choices.text: Take the mallet and begin

effects.log: It is two weeks of work and an unreasonable amount of tea. The roof goes up.

choices.text: Sit with Oksun and say nothing

effects.log: You sit. Something about the silence is helpful.

events.text: A wealthy young merchant has come to see {llg_thing} with servants, a poet and a plan: to have it all gilded. He has the permits. Oksun stands in front of him with her staff and is ignored. He asks you, as the one who appears to work here, where the gilders should begin. He wears a charm with the name of {llg_who} on it.

choices.text: Tell him where the real rot is, and send his silver there

effects.log: He is more embarrassed than offended. The money goes to the right beams.

choices.text: Talk him out of it, kindly

ok.log: You walk him round the whole place. By the end he is carrying a bucket. Oksun, passing, pats your arm.

fail.log: He is not persuaded. The gilders begin on the wrong side, and Oksun sighs for a season.

events.text: Oksun has grown frail. Perched on the step of {llg_thing}, she watches Kkachi hammer and tells you, uninvited, where her tools should go once she is gone. You jot it down. "You will be better at this than I," she says. It is not praise; it is a handing-over.

choices.text: Promise to keep the tools in use

effects.log: The promise is easy. Keeping it will take the rest of your life.

choices.text: Say she has years left yet

effects.log: She snorts. She does not have, and you both know it.

events.text: A broad-shouldered farmer with a boatman's hands comes to see you. Bae Mudol. His family has kept a reckoning for five generations, he says, and he has come to read it to someone, since the one who now tends {llg_thing} is the nearest to a responsible party. He sits down. He reads for three hours. It is all names and years. He never raises his voice.

choices.text: Hear it through to the end, and ask for a copy

effects.log: He gives you the copy. It is a worn thing, soft as cloth. You keep it.

choices.text: Tell him that it was all a very long time ago

effects.log: He looks at you for a moment. "Yes," he says. "That is what we all say, in the end." He leaves.

events.text: Bae Mudol has worked it out, or enough of it. Nobody knows how. He comes up the lane at dusk with a wood-axe, not hurrying, and says he is no fool and does not know how such things can be, but his grandmother told him what to look for. He says your hands are the same. He has come a long way. He sets the axe down between you.

choices.text: Kneel, and leave the axe where it is

effects.log: He looks at you for a long time. Then he takes the axe, and goes down the lane. It is not forgiveness. It is a start.

choices.text: Tell him what you have done with this life, and let him weigh it

ok.log: He listens to all of it. He weighs it. He nods once, and picks up the axe.

fail.log: He listens, and weighs it, and finds it light. He leaves the axe, which is a small mercy.

events.text: Word arrives from Bae Mudol: his daughter will keep the reckoning from now on, because he is weary and the ledger weighs too much. A solemn little girl with a satchel presents herself at the gate and asks leave to read out the first name. She reads it cleanly. She has rehearsed.

choices.text: Listen to all the names, however long it takes

effects.log: It takes an afternoon. She does not hurry, and neither do you.

choices.text: Ask her to read slowly, so you can remember them

effects.log: She slows. By dusk you can say a dozen of them yourself.

events.text: The family's reckoning has passed to its last keeper, an elderly woman who writes badly and reads by pointing. She hands you a spare copy, so that two households hold the record. The gesture is plain: a trust, a sentence, or both. You accept it with both hands.

choices.text: Promise to keep it where the next generation can find it

effects.log: You promise, and keep it, and the next generation does find it.

choices.text: Offer to add your own page at the end

effects.log: She nods, and gives you a pen. You write for an hour.

events.text: You have grown old tending {llg_thing}. The village has adopted you as a fixture; schoolchildren wave. At the evening supper an old pilgrim asks if the place is quiet. "It is," you say, and look at the stair, and for a moment know every foot that ever climbed it. The tea is hot. The air is clean.

choices.text: Sit a while longer

effects.log: The light turns gold. Somebody is sweeping, far off.

choices.text: Say good evening to the stair

effects.log: The stair does not answer. You do not mind.

events.text: Even in old age you are asked now and then to prove it, by eager young scholars with notebooks. You do. Some believe; some say "how splendid" and record something else. It has stopped bothering you. The place knows, and that suffices.

choices.text: Answer one more question, graciously

effects.log: You answer. The scholar writes it down, half-believing.

choices.text: Close the door gently on the notebook

effects.log: You close it. The lamp on the table is warm.

events.text: Your corrections have become the standard entry. The district rolls now carry them, and children learn the true dates. You pass through the records office once a year on pilgrimage. Nobody there knows you; the clerk bows at the door, and that is all it takes.

choices.text: Leave a small note on the desk of the clerk

effects.log: The note says only thanks. The clerk will puzzle over it for a week.

choices.text: Walk out into the evening

effects.log: The evening is mild. The rolls are right, and that is quietly enough.

events.text: Your hall still stands, slightly weathered. Children romp on the steps without a thought for the donor. The roof keeps out the rain. You sit on a bench across the lane with a mug of tea, and the roof is the finest thing you ever made.

choices.text: Pay for the next repair, quietly

effects.log: It is done by someone who does not ask. The roof holds.

choices.text: Watch the children

effects.log: They run in and out of the rain. You smile like a fool.

events.text: Atonement was the plan, and now age has come and the work stands unfinished, as it must. A newcomer has taken up the broom. You pass on what you know; they note it down and ask nothing more, which is all you could hope for.

choices.text: Hand over the broom

effects.log: It is lighter than you remembered. The younger one holds it with care.

choices.text: Keep sweeping, since you can still

effects.log: You sweep a little each morning. The lane is cleaner for it.

events.text: It is gone, the thing you tore down. Where it stood is a garden now, and a cloud of bees, and a little board nobody reads. You visit on warm days. The air is clear. You do not forgive yourself, but you have stopped waiting for the day you would.

choices.text: Sit among the bees

effects.log: They tolerate you. You doze a little.

choices.text: Pull a weed or two

effects.log: A small job, and good. The garden is yours to weed, if not to own.

events.text: You have not been back in some years. It still stands, you hear: {llg_thing}, in {llg_region}. Someone was telling it wrong at the inn only last week. You did not correct them. Then you got up and paid for the whole table, for reasons you kept to yourself, and went out into the cold feeling better than you had any right to.

choices.text: Walk home the long way

effects.log: The long way is longer than you remember. It is worth it.

choices.text: Go back in and hear the end

effects.log: The end is worse than the beginning, and better told.
